entries.title: Dynamic Code Evaluation Review
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.

Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

1. Prefer a library API or a fixed executable with a separate argument array; avoid passing external text to a shell.

entries.title: File Permission Review
entries.description: The code accesses, creates, deletes, or shares filesystem data. Resolve path provenance, destination containment, permission modes, and any concurrent access.
entries.impact: An attacker controlling a path or shared file may read or replace private files, delete data, or redirect an operation outside its intended directory if containment and access controls are ineffective.
entries.remediation:
Resolve paths beneath a fixed permitted root and verify containment and effective permissions. Use safe exclusive temporary-file creation, restrict sharing, and account for symlinks and concurrent changes.

Recommended actions:
1. Resolve paths against a fixed permitted root and enforce containment with filesystem-aware checks; avoid simple prefix checks.
2. Use application-controlled file identifiers where possible, restrict filesystem privileges, and test traversal and archive extraction boundaries.
entries.reviewer:
Verify the permission level is justified and the affected path cannot be exploited by a lower-privilege user. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace external influence over the path and resolve it as the filesystem will, including relative segments and symbolic links.
2. Check the resolved destination remains within the permitted root and that the caller is authorized for the specific file operation.
3. Inspect read, write and extraction paths separately; record the effective path restrictions and deployment permissions.

2. Verify reachable callers, external influence and effective protections, including deployment overrides and failure paths.
3. Record concrete evidence for a confirmed issue or a justified suppression; retain an unresolved outcome when the required evidence is unavailable.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: Shell Error Handling Review

entries.title: String Buffer Bounds Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling and Buffer Overflow
entries.description: The code calls a string-copy or formatting API without an explicit destination capacity. Review the actual buffer size, terminator space and source length for each call.
entries.impact: A write exceeding the destination capacity may corrupt memory or crash the process. The API call alone does not prove an overflow; constant strings and correctly sized buffers can be safe.
entries.remediation:
Prefer bounded operations and verify their size and termination contracts. Where an unbounded call remains, establish and test the destination-capacity invariant.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Compare the exact destination capacity with every possible input length. Do not infer either a vulnerability or a mitigation from unrelated calls elsewhere in the file.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: File Permission Review

entries.description: The code handles private data or configures build and process hardening. Determine which information is retained and what protection the deployed artifact actually supplies.
entries.impact: Insufficient memory, diagnostic, or build protections may make private values easier to recover or increase the consequences of another defect. Their absence alone does not establish an exploit path.
entries.remediation:
Minimize private data lifetimes and diagnostic exposure, apply the platform’s appropriate hardening controls, and verify the final binary rather than inferring protection from source markers alone.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.
2. Add a regression case for the unsafe condition and a valid protected case; verify the effective behavior in the relevant deployment.
entries.reviewer:

entries.title: Embedded Private Key Material
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
entries.reviewer:
Verify the secure handling of RSA private keys and assess if adequate measures are in place to safeguard their confidentiality and integrity. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.
2. Inspect how it is used and where it is exposed, including source history, build artifacts, logs and deployment configuration.
3. Record the affected service and privileges without copying secret values into the review report.

entries.title: Cleartext HTTP Communication Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Review all URLs or network requests across source code, configuration files, and external API references to ensure HTTPS is used instead of HTTP. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: Debug Information Review
entries.description: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Log only the operational details needed, redact sensitive values, and return limited error messages to clients.
2. Restrict diagnostic and log access and test production error responses and representative log output.
entries.reviewer:
Check for debug-related configurations in application settings and ensure that they are disabled or set to false in production environments to protect sensitive information. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched path logs sensitive data or exposes diagnostics to an untrusted recipient.
2. Trace the actual values, redaction and error handling, including production configuration and log retention or access.
3. Distinguish internal operational diagnostics from client-visible output and record the reachable disclosure path without reproducing secrets.

entries.title: SQL Injection Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that SQL queries use parameterized queries or prepared statements to handle user input securely. flag any occurrences of unsafe string concatenation in SQL queries for further review. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: IP Address Usage Review
entries.description: A syntactically valid address literal occurs outside recognized version metadata or source-code syntax. An address occurrence is a review surface, not a vulnerability.
entries.impact: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
entries.remediation:
Check the purpose of the address, how it is configured and which operations use it. For network destinations, review access policy, resolved addresses and deployment overrides. Do not treat every literal address as insecure.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.
2. Add a regression case for the unsafe condition and a valid protected case; verify the effective behavior in the relevant deployment.
entries.reviewer:
Verify the complete IPv4 or IPv6 value and its use as a destination, bind address, mask or access rule. Distinguish version metadata, regular-expression syntax and examples from active configuration. A literal alone does not prove exposure or a trust-boundary failure.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched construct in its containing function or configuration and identify the security-sensitive behavior under review.
2. Verify reachable callers, external influence and effective protections, including deployment overrides and failure paths.

entries.title: URL Usage Review
entries.description: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
entries.impact: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
entries.remediation:
Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.
2. Add a regression case for the unsafe condition and a valid protected case; verify the effective behavior in the relevant deployment.
entries.reviewer:
Verify the implementation of secure URL handling practices and assess if additional security measures are necessary. thoroughly investigate the presence of these URLs, determine their purpose, and ensure they undergo appropriate taint validation. Reviewers should pay special attention to URLs associated with data exfiltration concerns and assess the trustworthiness of third-party URLs to mitigate potential security risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched construct in its containing function or configuration and identify the security-sensitive behavior under review.
2. Verify reachable callers, external influence and effective protections, including deployment overrides and failure paths.
3. Record concrete evidence for a confirmed issue or a justified suppression; retain an unresolved outcome when the required evidence is unavailable.

entries.title: Redirect Destination Review
entries.description: The code handles a link, redirect, or externally selected navigation target. Validate the effective destination and any action triggered by the receiving handler.
entries.impact: A crafted destination or link may direct users to a phishing site, leak URL-carried secrets, or trigger unauthorized operations if routing trusts external parameters without the required access checks.
entries.remediation:
Allowlist schemes, hosts, paths, and operations. Validate parsed link parameters, avoid credentials in URLs, and require authentication and authorization before sensitive actions.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer application route identifiers mapped to fixed destinations; permit only necessary relative paths or explicitly allowed external destinations.
2. Reject unsupported schemes and ambiguous destinations and test redirect handling after decoding and normalization.
entries.reviewer:
Review the code for potential unvalidated redirect and forward vulnerabilities and verify if proper input validation and destination checks are implemented. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether untrusted input controls the redirect destination and whether the redirect is reachable.
2. Inspect URL parsing, relative versus absolute destinations, scheme handling and authorization around the redirect.
3. Check how encoded or ambiguous URLs are interpreted by the framework and browser before confirming an unsafe redirect.

entries.title: API Endpoint Review
entries.description: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
entries.impact: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
entries.remediation:

Recommended actions:

entries.reviewer:
Check for the presence of API endpoints in the source code. Verify if developers have implemented appropriate security measures for handling API endpoints, such as input validation, authentication, authorization, rate limiting, and secure data handling. Also assess the sensitivity of the data handled by the API endpoints and confirm the presence of relevant security controls. entries.title: TODO Comments
entries.description: The code contains a maintainability, accessibility, or build-configuration review marker. Establish a concrete affected behavior before assigning security severity.
entries.impact: No direct confidentiality or integrity consequence is established by this marker alone. A related implementation defect could affect availability or prevent users from using essential controls, depending on the actual behavior.
entries.remediation:
Resolve the specific unfinished behavior, accessibility requirement, or build hygiene concern. Confirm its real operational effect and test the corrected behavior before classifying it as a security defect.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.
2. Add a regression case for the unsafe condition and a valid protected case; verify the effective behavior in the relevant deployment.
entries.reviewer:
Check for the presence of TODO comments and verify if they have been properly addressed during code reviews and inspections. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched construct in its containing function or configuration and identify the security-sensitive behavior under review.
2. Verify reachable callers, external influence and effective protections, including deployment overrides and failure paths.
3. Record concrete evidence for a confirmed issue or a justified suppression; retain an unresolved outcome when the required evidence is unavailable.

entries.title: Monkey Patching Review
entries.description: The code obtains executable material or replaces application behavior at runtime. Determine the origin, integrity checks, and intended deployment scope.
entries.impact: A party able to substitute executable material or a runtime hook may run code with application privileges, inspect protected data, or alter security checks.
entries.remediation:
Load only approved code from trusted locations, verify signatures or integrity before execution, and restrict runtime replacement to documented, authorized behavior.

Recommended actions:
1. Use trusted distribution channels and verify authenticity and integrity before executing downloaded material.
2. Restrict allowed sources and execution capabilities and test that failed verification prevents loading or execution.
entries.reviewer:
Verify the presence of monkey patched code in the project and assess its impact on code stability and security. Particular attention should be paid to patches affecting security-critical components like authentication, authorization, or database queries. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace the origin of downloaded or dynamically loaded code and inspect its integrity and publisher verification.
2. Check which privileges the loaded material receives and whether external input can change the source or verification policy.
3. Verify failure behavior when integrity or authenticity checks fail; dynamic loading alone does not establish compromise.

entries.title: Cryptographic Algorithm Use Review
entries.description: The checked source uses a random generator, cryptographic primitive, or initialization value whose suitability depends on its security purpose and inputs.
entries.impact: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.

Recommended actions:
1. Use maintained high-level cryptographic APIs appropriate to the purpose; use authenticated encryption for confidential application data.
2. For passwords, use the platform password-hashing facility rather than a fast general-purpose digest. Verify key, nonce and migration handling for affected data.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that secure cryptographic algorithms are used to mitigate the risk of cryptographic vulnerabilities. Assess whether deprecated or weak algorithms are used and recommend replacing them with stronger alternatives. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the purpose of the cryptographic operation, algorithm, mode, key or nonce handling, and protected data.
2. Distinguish password storage, confidentiality, integrity and non-security checksums; each requires different controls.
3. Inspect deployed configuration and all encrypt, decrypt or verification paths before deciding whether the use is unsafe.

entries.title: Security Control Bypass Review
entries.description: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
entries.impact: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.
entries.remediation:
Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.

Recommended actions:
1. Use a trusted verifier and enforce the applicable server-side identity and resource checks consistently.
2. Fail closed on invalid evidence and test that alternate routes and error paths cannot issue unintended access.
entries.reviewer:
Investigate any matches for backdoor-related terms, ensuring that no actual backdoor entries or bypass techniques exist in the code. They must verify that proper security measures are implemented to prevent unauthorized access and assess the overall security posture of the application. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the trusted identity verifier, protected resources and decision made by the matched control.
2. Inspect effective middleware and service checks, alternate routes and failure paths; validate the supplied evidence before issuing privileges.
3. Test invalid identity evidence, insufficient permissions and access to another user or tenant before confirming a bypass.

entries.title: CAPTCHA Review
entries.description: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
entries.impact: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.
entries.remediation:
Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.

Recommended actions:
1. Use a trusted verifier and enforce the applicable server-side identity and resource checks consistently.
2. Fail closed on invalid evidence and test that alternate routes and error paths cannot issue unintended access.
entries.reviewer:
Assess the strength and security of the CAPTCHA implementation to ensure it provides adequate protection against automated or malicious activities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the trusted identity verifier, protected resources and decision made by the matched control.
2. Inspect effective middleware and service checks, alternate routes and failure paths; validate the supplied evidence before issuing privileges.
3. Test invalid identity evidence, insufficient permissions and access to another user or tenant before confirming a bypass.

entries.title: Security Control Review
entries.description: The code contains a security-control marker. Its presence is a review surface rather than evidence that the control is defective or consistently enforced.
entries.impact: No adverse security consequence follows from the presence of a protection alone. If it is bypassed or applied outside the correct context, the protected operation may still permit injection or unauthorized access.
entries.remediation:
Verify that the control applies to every relevant entry point and uses the required context and policy. Retain effective protections; test bypass cases before recommending a change.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Evaluate the effectiveness of the standard mitigation techniques and assess if additional measures are necessary for robust security. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: Untrusted Input Entry Point
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code accepts or reads externally influenced data. Trace it to security-sensitive operations and identify the validation and authorization required by each destination.
entries.impact: External input may cause injection, incorrect decisions, or unauthorized data access if it reaches a sensitive operation without the controls required by that operation. Reading input alone does not establish a vulnerability.
entries.remediation:
Validate type, size, and allowed values at trust boundaries, and apply destination-specific parameter binding or output encoding. Enforce authorization independently of input validation.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Reviewers should ensure proper input handling for functions like `cin` or `getline`. Confirm that developers have implemented input validation techniques to handle edge cases and ensure safe processing. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: OS Command Injection Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Reviewers should ensure that calls to command execution functions are justified, that inputs are thoroughly sanitized, and that safer alternatives are considered. Look for proper error handling and minimal privileges when interacting with system resources. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Loop Bounds Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code manages allocation, ownership, indexed access, or resource release. Confirm capacity, lifetime, nullability, and transfer of ownership across callers.
entries.impact: An invalid lifetime or out-of-range access may corrupt memory, disclose process data, or crash the application. Unbounded or unreleased resources may exhaust memory and deny service under repeated use.
entries.remediation:
Enforce bounds and lifetime invariants, handle allocation failure, and use appropriate automatic resource ownership. Confirm a leak or invalid access before adding cleanup that could introduce double release.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Ensure all loops use proper bounds to avoid access violations. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Memory Copy Size and Overlap Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code copies a caller-specified amount of native memory. Verify source and destination extents, length arithmetic and the API's overlap contract.
entries.impact: An incorrect copy length or overlapping memcpy regions may cause invalid reads or writes, corrupt state, disclose memory or crash the process. A correctly bounded copy is legitimate; this review marker alone does not establish a vulnerability.
entries.remediation:
Check both buffer capacities and guard size multiplication or addition before allocation and copying. Use memmove where overlap is possible and retain explicit ownership and lifetime guarantees.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Trace each copy length to image dimensions, file metadata or caller input. Compare it with both allocation sizes and review integer overflow, truncation, lifetime and overlap.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: String Buffer Bounds Review
entries.description: The code calls a string-copy or formatting API without an explicit destination capacity. Review the actual buffer size, terminator space and source length for each call.
entries.impact: A write exceeding the destination capacity may corrupt memory or crash the process. The API call alone does not prove an overflow; constant strings and correctly sized buffers can be safe.
entries.remediation:
Prefer bounded operations and verify their size and termination contracts. Where an unbounded call remains, establish and test the destination-capacity invariant.

Recommended actions:
1. Use bounded operations, checked size calculations and explicit ownership or automatic resource management appropriate to the language.
2. Test boundary sizes and failure paths; use memory diagnostics where available to verify the specific correction.
entries.reviewer:
Compare the exact destination capacity with every possible input length. Do not infer either a vulnerability or a mitigation from unrelated calls elsewhere in the file.

Review steps:
1. Inspect buffer capacity, index bounds, integer conversions and ownership at the matched operation and its callers.
2. Check initialization, aliases, lifetime and cleanup on success, exception and early-return paths; identify external influence over sizes or values.
3. Verify a concrete unsafe access or lifetime condition. A low-level API or allocation alone does not prove memory corruption.

entries.title: Container Bounds Review
entries.description: The code performs checked vector indexing. Verify index provenance and handling of the std::out_of_range exception; at() itself performs a bounds check.
entries.impact: An unhandled out-of-range exception may terminate the operation or process and affect availability. The checked accessor alone does not establish a buffer overflow or undefined behavior.
entries.remediation:
Validate external indexes against the current vector size and handle expected range failures at the appropriate boundary. Retain checked access rather than replacing it with unchecked indexing.

Review steps:

3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Server-Side Request Forgery Review
entries.description: The application makes an outbound request whose destination may be influenced by external data. Resolve URL construction, redirects, DNS results, and network reachability.
entries.impact: If an attacker can select a reachable destination, the application may expose internal services or metadata credentials, or send protected data to an unauthorized recipient.
entries.remediation:
Allowlist required destinations and protocols, validate resolved addresses and every redirect, and restrict outbound access to internal and metadata services.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer fixed destinations or a restricted set of permitted services; validate schemes, hosts and ports before the request.
2. Apply destination checks to redirects and resolved addresses where applicable, restrict network egress, and test prohibited destinations.
entries.reviewer:
Trace the request argument, BaseAddress, redirects and resolved destination. Verify who controls each value and whether destination restrictions apply to this request. A request operation alone is not proof of external control or exploitability.

Review steps:
1. Verify the operation makes a server-side request, then trace external control over the URL, host, port and redirects.
2. Inspect destination restrictions, DNS resolution and redirect handling; distinguish fixed destinations from caller-controlled requests.
3. Check deployment egress controls and whether internal services or local files are reachable from the requesting process.

entries.title: LDAP Injection Review
entries.description: The code constructs a directory query, XPath expression, or naming-service lookup. Review which input controls query syntax or the lookup target.
entries.impact: Attacker-controlled query syntax may bypass intended selection or authorization and expose protected records. An attacker-selected naming-service target may also invoke unsafe remote resolution, depending on runtime behavior.
entries.remediation:
Keep untrusted values out of expression structure and remote naming targets. Use context-appropriate parameter binding or escaping, fixed trusted lookup destinations, and least-privileged service credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Use the query API’s parameter mechanism or syntax-specific escaping for data values; restrict externally selected lookup destinations.
2. Test that unusual input cannot alter query structure or bypass access controls; avoid substituting generic sanitization for the required control.
entries.reviewer:
Verify LDAP filter construction escapes all user-supplied components. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect how untrusted values enter the directory query, selection expression or naming-service lookup.
2. Distinguish data parameters from syntax and determine whether external input can alter the selected records or remote target.
3. Verify the exact API-specific escaping, binding or destination restrictions and resource authorization at the use point.

entries.title: Password Comparison Review
entries.description: A credential expression is compared with itself. Inspect authentication control flow and whether the supplied credential is checked.
entries.impact: An equality check against the same stored value may bypass credential verification if it controls an authentication decision. Reachability must be confirmed.
entries.remediation:
Compare the supplied credential with the expected value using the intended verification routine. Test wrong credentials and each authentication path.

Recommended actions:
1. Use the established authentication mechanism consistently and fail closed when credentials or provider responses are invalid.
2. Remove bypass paths, avoid revealing credential-validation details to clients, and test that failed authentication cannot create an authenticated session.
entries.reviewer:
Review the recorded operation and authentication call sites; a rule match is not proof of exploitation.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the complete login or credential-validation path, including alternate providers, error paths and session issuance.
2. Verify that credential checks operate on the supplied and stored values and that bypass conditions are unreachable in production.
3. Record effective authentication middleware and test invalid credentials and unauthorized session creation.

entries.title: Reversible Password Storage
entries.description: An encryption or decryption operation appears in a password-processing function. Inspect its use as password storage.
entries.impact: A stored password may be recoverable with the encryption key. Credential storage should use a salted adaptive password hash.
entries.remediation:
Replace reversible password storage with a maintained password-hashing implementation. Review key exposure and plan a controlled migration.

Recommended actions:
1. Use maintained high-level cryptographic APIs appropriate to the purpose; use authenticated encryption for confidential application data.
2. For passwords, use the platform password-hashing facility rather than a fast general-purpose digest. Verify key, nonce and migration handling for affected data.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Identify the purpose of the cryptographic operation, algorithm, mode, key or nonce handling, and protected data.
2. Distinguish password storage, confidentiality, integrity and non-security checksums; each requires different controls.
3. Inspect deployed configuration and all encrypt, decrypt or verification paths before deciding whether the use is unsafe.

entries.title: JWT Claims Validation Review
entries.description: A method reads decoded JWT claims without a local token-validation call. Verify signature validation and middleware before trusting claims.
entries.impact: Decoding a token does not establish its authenticity. Trusting unvalidated claims can permit impersonation; validation elsewhere must be reviewed before confirming a defect.
entries.remediation:
Obtain identity from a validated principal or validate the token against the intended signing key, issuer, audience and lifetime before using its claims.

Recommended actions:
1. Use a trusted verifier and enforce the applicable server-side identity and resource checks consistently.
2. Fail closed on invalid evidence and test that alternate routes and error paths cannot issue unintended access.
entries.reviewer:
Trace the decoded claims into authentication or authorization decisions and verify the endpoint middleware. A missing local validation call alone does not prove bypass. Unrelated or later validation, validation in a conditional branch, and an unchecked asynchronous validation result do not protect this decode site. Verify the same token and successful validation on every path before consuming identity.

Review steps:
1. Identify the trusted identity verifier, protected resources and decision made by the matched control.
2. Inspect effective middleware and service checks, alternate routes and failure paths; validate the supplied evidence before issuing privileges.
3. Test invalid identity evidence, insufficient permissions and access to another user or tenant before confirming a bypass.

entries.title: JWT Validation Policy Review
entries.description: A token-policy setting disables an issuer, audience, lifetime, signing-key policy or signed-token requirement. Review the actual policy object and the values accepted by each endpoint. A false flag does not by itself establish authentication bypass.
entries.impact: An endpoint may accept tokens outside the intended issuer, audience or validity period, or permit unsigned tokens when RequireSignedTokens is disabled. entries.remediation:

Recommended actions:
1. Use a trusted verifier and enforce the applicable server-side identity and resource checks consistently.
2. Fail closed on invalid evidence and test that alternate routes and error paths cannot issue unintended access.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect the active TokenValidationParameters instance, custom validators and middleware order. A development/test keyword or a strong policy elsewhere does not protect this setting. Verify RequireSignedTokens separately from ValidateIssuerSigningKey.

Review steps:
1. Identify the trusted identity verifier, protected resources and decision made by the matched control.
2. Inspect effective middleware and service checks, alternate routes and failure paths; validate the supplied evidence before issuing privileges.
3. Test invalid identity evidence, insufficient permissions and access to another user or tenant before confirming a bypass.

entries.title: Developer Exception Page Enabled
entries.description: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Disable development-only functionality in production and enforce the environment boundary in deployment configuration.
2. Restrict operational diagnostics and add a production-configuration check covering the exposed route or feature.
entries.reviewer:
Verify environment guard around UseDeveloperExceptionPage. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:

2. Check environment guards, deployment overrides and the information or capabilities exposed by the feature.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect all HTTP client handlers for certificate bypass. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: SQL Query Construction Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Review callsites for untrusted argument flow. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: Cross-Origin Access Policy Review
entries.description: A browser-origin or navigation policy permits a broad set of external origins or destinations. Identify the resources and privileged interfaces covered by the effective policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted site may read protected responses or invoke privileged interfaces if a permissive policy admits it and independent authentication or authorization does not prevent the operation.
entries.remediation:
Allow only required trusted origins and destinations. Validate origin and message schemas, handle credentials deliberately, and enforce access controls independently of the origin policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Allow only the origins and browser capabilities required by the application; avoid reflecting arbitrary origins.
2. Test both preflight and actual responses and ensure authentication and authorization remain enforced independently of CORS.
entries.reviewer:
Verify policy registration and environment overrides. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective origin policy together with credentials, allowed methods and headers, including environment overrides.
2. Determine which sensitive responses are exposed to browsers and whether origins are reflected or broadly trusted.
3. Test preflight and actual responses using an unapproved origin; a broad policy alone does not prove access to protected data.

entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.
2. Inspect how it is used and where it is exposed, including source history, build artifacts, logs and deployment configuration.
3. Record the affected service and privileges without copying secret values into the review report.

entries.impact: A predictable fallback used as an active key can enable forgery or disclosure. A fixture, unused value or non-secret identifier does not establish that impact.
entries.remediation:
Fail closed when required security configuration is missing; load production keys from an appropriate secret store and verify the failure path.

Recommended actions:

entries.title: Developer Exception Page Enabled
entries.description: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Disable development-only functionality in production and enforce the environment boundary in deployment configuration.
2. Restrict operational diagnostics and add a production-configuration check covering the exposed route or feature.
entries.reviewer:
Verify environment guard around UseDeveloperExceptionPage. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective production configuration and determine who can reach debugging or development functionality.
2. Check environment guards, deployment overrides and the information or capabilities exposed by the feature.
3. Verify the actual production behavior; a development-only setting is not itself a production vulnerability.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect all HTTP client handlers for certificate bypass. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: SQL Query Construction Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Review callsites for untrusted argument flow. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: Cross-Origin Access Policy Review
entries.description: A browser-origin or navigation policy permits a broad set of external origins or destinations. Identify the resources and privileged interfaces covered by the effective policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted site may read protected responses or invoke privileged interfaces if a permissive policy admits it and independent authentication or authorization does not prevent the operation.
entries.remediation:
Allow only required trusted origins and destinations. Validate origin and message schemas, handle credentials deliberately, and enforce access controls independently of the origin policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Allow only the origins and browser capabilities required by the application; avoid reflecting arbitrary origins.
2. Test both preflight and actual responses and ensure authentication and authorization remain enforced independently of CORS.
entries.reviewer:
Verify policy registration and environment overrides. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective origin policy together with credentials, allowed methods and headers, including environment overrides.
2. Determine which sensitive responses are exposed to browsers and whether origins are reflected or broadly trusted.
3. Test preflight and actual responses using an unapproved origin; a broad policy alone does not prove access to protected data.

entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
entries.reviewer:
Review secret handling and rotate exposed values. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.
2. Inspect how it is used and where it is exposed, including source history, build artifacts, logs and deployment configuration.
3. Record the affected service and privileges without copying secret values into the review report.

entries.title: Password Policy Review
entries.description: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
entries.impact: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.
entries.remediation:
Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.

Recommended actions:
1. Use a trusted verifier and enforce the applicable server-side identity and resource checks consistently.
2. Fail closed on invalid evidence and test that alternate routes and error paths cannot issue unintended access.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm password options meet current security standards (NIST SP 800-63B recommends minimum 8 characters; 12+ is preferred). This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the trusted identity verifier, protected resources and decision made by the matched control.
2. Inspect effective middleware and service checks, alternate routes and failure paths; validate the supplied evidence before issuing privileges.
3. Test invalid identity evidence, insufficient permissions and access to another user or tenant before confirming a bypass.

entries.title: JWT Validation Policy Review
entries.description: A token-policy setting disables an issuer, audience, lifetime, signing-key policy or signed-token requirement. Review the actual policy object and the values accepted by each endpoint. A false flag does not by itself establish authentication bypass.
entries.impact: An endpoint may accept tokens outside the intended issuer, audience or validity period, or permit unsigned tokens when RequireSignedTokens is disabled. ValidateIssuerSigningKey controls signing-key policy validation; setting it false alone does not establish that signature verification is disabled.
entries.remediation:
Configure token validation for the intended trust boundary and verify invalid-token rejection. Keep issuer and audience restrictions appropriate to the endpoint, enforce lifetime and signed-token requirements, and validate signing-key policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Use a trusted verifier and enforce the applicable server-side identity and resource checks consistently.
2. Fail closed on invalid evidence and test that alternate routes and error paths cannot issue unintended access.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect the active TokenValidationParameters instance, custom validators and middleware order. A development/test keyword or a strong policy elsewhere does not protect this setting. Verify RequireSignedTokens separately from ValidateIssuerSigningKey.

Review steps:
1. Identify the trusted identity verifier, protected resources and decision made by the matched control.
2. Inspect effective middleware and service checks, alternate routes and failure paths; validate the supplied evidence before issuing privileges.
3. Test invalid identity evidence, insufficient permissions and access to another user or tenant before confirming a bypass.

entries.title: Authentication Review
entries.description: A file or directory name matches the authentication review area. This check inspects paths, not the implementation or a reachable execution path.
entries.impact: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness. A filename match alone does not establish this consequence.
entries.remediation:
Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.

Recommended actions:
1. Where exposure is verified, remove unnecessary files from deployment or restrict access to the intended users and processes.
2. Verify the deployed artifact and access behavior after the change; retain required application files with appropriate controls.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched file or directory contents and determine whether it is deployed or externally accessible.
2. Identify whether sensitive data, configuration or executable content is present; a name match alone does not establish exposure.
3. Check effective access controls and build or packaging exclusions and record the specific content and exposure path.

entries.impact: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness. A filename match alone does not establish this consequence.
entries.remediation:
Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.

Recommended actions:
1. Where exposure is verified, remove unnecessary files from deployment or restrict access to the intended users and processes.
2. Verify the deployed artifact and access behavior after the change; retain required application files with appropriate controls.
entries.reviewer:
Verify the presence and correctness of user section-related code paths. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched file or directory contents and determine whether it is deployed or externally accessible.
2. Identify whether sensitive data, configuration or executable content is present; a name match alone does not establish exposure.
3. Check effective access controls and build or packaging exclusions and record the specific content and exposure path.

entries.title: Debug Mode Configuration Review
entries.description: A configuration or API enables development diagnostics, process inspection, or debugging. Verify whether it applies to a deployed production artifact.
entries.impact: An actor with access to an enabled debugging interface may inspect private state or influence application execution; exposed development endpoints may disclose internal implementation details.
entries.remediation:
Disable debugging and development endpoints in production, bind necessary diagnostic services to restricted interfaces, and verify the final deployed artifact and access policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Disable development-only functionality in production and enforce the environment boundary in deployment configuration.
2. Restrict operational diagnostics and add a production-configuration check covering the exposed route or feature.
entries.reviewer:
Verify framework mode defaults in production runtime. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective production configuration and determine who can reach debugging or development functionality.
2. Check environment guards, deployment overrides and the information or capabilities exposed by the feature.
3. Verify the actual production behavior; a development-only setting is not itself a production vulnerability.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect all transport/client configs for bypass settings. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: SQL Injection Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Trace user input into query format strings. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: Cross-Origin Access Policy Review
entries.description: A browser-origin or navigation policy permits a broad set of external origins or destinations. Identify the resources and privileged interfaces covered by the effective policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted site may read protected responses or invoke privileged interfaces if a permissive policy admits it and independent authentication or authorization does not prevent the operation.
entries.remediation:
Allow only required trusted origins and destinations. Validate origin and message schemas, handle credentials deliberately, and enforce access controls independently of the origin policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Allow only the origins and browser capabilities required by the application; avoid reflecting arbitrary origins.
2. Test both preflight and actual responses and ensure authentication and authorization remain enforced independently of CORS.
entries.reviewer:
Validate CORS policy builders and middleware config. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective origin policy together with credentials, allowed methods and headers, including environment overrides.
2. Determine which sensitive responses are exposed to browsers and whether origins are reflected or broadly trusted.
3. Test preflight and actual responses using an unapproved origin; a broad policy alone does not prove access to protected data.

entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm no production secrets are committed. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.
2. Inspect how it is used and where it is exposed, including source history, build artifacts, logs and deployment configuration.
3. Record the affected service and privileges without copying secret values into the review report.

entries.title: Security Configuration Fallback Review
entries.description: Security-named configuration has a literal fallback candidate. Determine whether that value reaches a cryptographic key or an authentication secret.
entries.impact: A predictable fallback used as an active key can enable forgery or disclosure. A fixture, unused value or non-secret identifier does not establish that impact.
entries.remediation:
Fail closed when required security configuration is missing; load production keys from an appropriate secret store and verify the failure path.

Recommended actions:
1. Fail closed when required security configuration is missing; load production keys from an appropriate secret store and verify the failure path.
entries.reviewer:
Verify the exact source, operation and applicable controls. This is a review candidate, not a confirmed vulnerability.

Review steps:
1. Security-named configuration has a literal fallback candidate. Determine whether that value reaches a cryptographic key or an authentication secret.
2. Check the control on the actual path; unrelated markers must not suppress the candidate.

entries.description: The code disables, exempts, or configures request-forgery protection. Verify whether a reachable state-changing operation authenticates through automatically sent browser credentials.

Confirm CSRF middleware is applied to all POST/PUT/DELETE/PATCH routes with Secure cookies. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.
