entries.impact: Weak session secrets, exposed cookies, or inadequate expiry may allow session theft, token forgery, or continued access after the user’s intended authorization ends.
entries.remediation:
Use strong unpredictable session secrets, rotate tokens on privilege changes, and enforce expiry and revocation. Set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite attributes for sensitive browser cookies.

Recommended actions:
1. Set cookie protections appropriate to its purpose and deployed HTTPS flow; keep sensitive session cookies inaccessible to scripts where required.
2. Limit cookie scope and lifetime, rotate sessions at authentication changes, and test actual browser and response-header behavior.

Review steps:

2. Check effective Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite behavior, domain and path scope, expiry and session rotation in the deployed flow.
3. Distinguish intended browser access from a missing protection; verify actual response headers and cross-site behavior.

entries.impact: An attacker-selected origin can expose sensitive browser-readable responses if the effective policy and resource access permit it.
entries.remediation:
Use exact approved origins and verify credentialed preflight and actual responses. Authentication and authorization remain independent controls.

Recommended actions:
1. Use exact approved origins and verify credentialed preflight and actual responses. Authentication and authorization remain independent controls.

entries.title: Tenant Data Constraint Review

entries.remediation:
Derive the effective tenant from trusted authenticated context, apply it to the exact data operation and verify access using two distinct tenants.

entries.title: Untrusted Input Entry Point
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code accepts or reads externally influenced data. Trace it to security-sensitive operations and identify the validation and authorization required by each destination.
entries.impact: External input may cause injection, incorrect decisions, or unauthorized data access if it reaches a sensitive operation without the controls required by that operation. Reading input alone does not establish a vulnerability.
entries.remediation:
Validate type, size, and allowed values at trust boundaries, and apply destination-specific parameter binding or output encoding. Enforce authorization independently of input validation.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Ensure that proper input handling is in place for HTTP request parameters. Verify that developers have implemented appropriate input validation and sanitization techniques to prevent security vulnerabilities related to untrusted inputs. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: OS Command Injection Review
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer a library API or a fixed executable with a separate argument array; avoid passing external text to a shell.
2. Restrict permitted operations and arguments, constrain option handling, and test rejected input under the actual deployment privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Check for the secure usage of shell-executing functions and assess if user input is properly validated, sanitized, and appropriately used as command parameters. Ensure that developers have implemented strong input validation measures, command parameterization techniques, and proper context-aware security controls to mitigate command injection vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the executable, arguments, shell use and working directory; trace external influence over each.
2. Check whether a shell interprets metacharacters or whether options can change command behavior even without a shell.
3. Verify the operation is reachable and examine validation, executable selection and process privileges before confirming an issue.

entries.title: Go Unsafe Code Review
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

Recommended actions:
1. Replace externally assembled code with fixed operations and data-only inputs where possible.
2. Keep template or expression sources under application control; restrict exposed capabilities and test rejection of unexpected syntax.
entries.reviewer:
Check for the secure usage of unsafe code execution mechanisms and assess if user input is properly validated, sanitized, and appropriately used. Ensure that developers have implemented strong input validation measures and proper context-aware security controls to mitigate arbitrary code execution vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched operation interprets code, expressions or templates; identify its execution context and permissions.
2. Trace control over the executed text and distinguish fixed application code from externally influenced content.
3. Inspect restrictions and failure paths; record a reachable input-to-execution path before confirming code execution.

entries.title: HTML Output Encoding Review
entries.description: The code contains a security-control marker. Its presence is a review surface rather than evidence that the control is defective or consistently enforced.
entries.impact: No adverse security consequence follows from the presence of a protection alone. If it is bypassed or applied outside the correct context, the protected operation may still permit injection or unauthorized access.
entries.remediation:
Verify that the control applies to every relevant entry point and uses the required context and policy. Retain effective protections; test bypass cases before recommending a change.

Recommended actions:
1. Use safe text or template APIs and context-appropriate encoding at the rendering boundary.
2. If rich HTML is required, use a maintained sanitizer with a restricted policy; validate URL schemes and test the actual browser output.
entries.reviewer:
Assess whether Go-specific output encoding or sanitization is applied consistently before user-controlled data reaches HTML output. Confirm the defense is appropriate for the rendering context and that reachable paths do not bypass it. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace the matched value to its browser rendering context: text, attribute, URL, script or DOM operation.
2. Inspect the exact encoder or safe rendering API and any bypass of automatic escaping; verify it protects that context.
3. Distinguish literal trusted content from externally influenced markup. Record the reachable rendering path and any effective sanitizer configuration.

entries.title: Password Hashing Review
entries.description: Fast hashing is used inside a password-processing function. Review whether password storage uses a salted, adaptive password hash.
entries.impact: Offline password guessing can be cheaper when passwords use a fast general-purpose hash. This review condition does not establish database exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use a maintained adaptive password-hashing implementation with a per-password salt and an appropriate work factor; migrate stored hashes on authentication.

Recommended actions:
1. Use maintained high-level cryptographic APIs appropriate to the purpose; use authenticated encryption for confidential application data.
2. For passwords, use the platform password-hashing facility rather than a fast general-purpose digest. Verify key, nonce and migration handling for affected data.
entries.reviewer:
Review the recorded operation and authentication call sites; a rule match is not proof of exploitation.

Review steps:
1. Identify the purpose of the cryptographic operation, algorithm, mode, key or nonce handling, and protected data.
2. Distinguish password storage, confidentiality, integrity and non-security checksums; each requires different controls.
3. Inspect deployed configuration and all encrypt, decrypt or verification paths before deciding whether the use is unsafe.

entries.title: Security Configuration Fallback Review
entries.description: Security-named configuration has a literal fallback candidate. Determine whether that value reaches a cryptographic key or an authentication secret.
entries.impact: A predictable fallback used as an active key can enable forgery or disclosure. A fixture, unused value or non-secret identifier does not establish that impact.
entries.remediation:
Fail closed when required security configuration is missing; load production keys from an appropriate secret store and verify the failure path.

Recommended actions:
1. Fail closed when required security configuration is missing; load production keys from an appropriate secret store and verify the failure path.

entries.title: Management Endpoint Exposure Review
entries.description: Management endpoint configuration may expose operational interfaces. Resolve which endpoints are enabled, externally reachable, and protected.
entries.impact: Unauthorized callers may obtain operational details or invoke administrative actions if exposed management endpoints lack effective access controls.
entries.remediation:
Expose only required management endpoints on restricted interfaces, apply explicit authentication and authorization, and disable unnecessary administrative or diagnostic operations.

Recommended actions:
1. Disable development-only functionality in production and enforce the environment boundary in deployment configuration.
2. Restrict operational diagnostics and add a production-configuration check covering the exposed route or feature.
entries.reviewer:
Verify actuator/management endpoints are hardened in production. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective production configuration and determine who can reach debugging or development functionality.
2. Check environment guards, deployment overrides and the information or capabilities exposed by the feature.
3. Verify the actual production behavior; a development-only setting is not itself a production vulnerability.

entries.title: SQL Injection Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect tainted data flow into query construction APIs. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: Cross-Origin Access Policy Review
entries.description: A browser-origin or navigation policy permits a broad set of external origins or destinations. Identify the resources and privileged interfaces covered by the effective policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted site may read protected responses or invoke privileged interfaces if a permissive policy admits it and independent authentication or authorization does not prevent the operation.
entries.remediation:
Allow only required trusted origins and destinations. Validate origin and message schemas, handle credentials deliberately, and enforce access controls independently of the origin policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Allow only the origins and browser capabilities required by the application; avoid reflecting arbitrary origins.
2. Test both preflight and actual responses and ensure authentication and authorization remain enforced independently of CORS.
entries.reviewer:
Validate CORS settings across all controllers and profiles. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective origin policy together with credentials, allowed methods and headers, including environment overrides.
2. Determine which sensitive responses are exposed to browsers and whether origins are reflected or broadly trusted.
3. Test preflight and actual responses using an unapproved origin; a broad policy alone does not prove access to protected data.

entries.title: Cleartext HTTP Communication Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Review transport settings for production hardening. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
entries.reviewer:
Verify credentials are not stored in source/config. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.
2. Inspect how it is used and where it is exposed, including source history, build artifacts, logs and deployment configuration.
3. Record the affected service and privileges without copying secret values into the review report.

entries.title: Explicit Anonymous Operation Review
entries.description: An explicit anonymous-access declaration is present. Associate it with the affected route and operations, including inherited policy requirements.
entries.impact: Public access is often intentional. A defect exists only if the reachable operation requires identity or resource permissions that are not enforced.
entries.remediation:
Declare public entry points intentionally and enforce the required resource permissions at sensitive operations. Test neighboring protected routes and override behavior.

Recommended actions:
1. Declare public entry points intentionally and enforce the required resource permissions at sensitive operations. Test neighboring protected routes and override behavior.

entries.title: SQL Injection Review

entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code accepts or reads externally influenced data. Trace it to security-sensitive operations and identify the validation and authorization required by each destination.
entries.impact: External input may cause injection, incorrect decisions, or unauthorized data access if it reaches a sensitive operation without the controls required by that operation. Reading input alone does not establish a vulnerability.
entries.remediation:
Validate type, size, and allowed values at trust boundaries, and apply destination-specific parameter binding or output encoding. Enforce authorization independently of input validation.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Ensure that proper input handling is in place for `requestParameters`. Verify that developers have implemented appropriate input validation and sanitization techniques to prevent security vulnerabilities related to untrusted inputs. Also assess the sensitivity of the data handled through `requestParameters` and confirm that relevant security measures, such as output encoding and protection against injection attacks, are implemented correctly. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: SQL Injection Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that Java code uses prepared statements or parameterized queries to prevent SQL injection. Also assess the overall security of the database interactions and confirm that proper input validation and sanitization techniques are implemented. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

entries.title: Object Serialization Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The application reads serialized objects or uses a parser that may construct runtime types. Identify the input’s trust and the effective parser and type restrictions.
entries.impact: A crafted untrusted payload may instantiate dangerous types or trigger object behavior that executes code, modifies state, or exhausts resources when the parser permits those operations.
entries.remediation:
Use a data-only format and a safe loader for untrusted input. Disable automatic object or type construction, allowlist required types, and bound parsing size and complexity.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that appropriate measures are taken to mitigate serialization/deserialization vulnerabilities. Ensure that input validation, integrity checks, and secure coding practices are implemented for serialization and deserialization operations. Also assess the sensitivity of the serialized data and confirm that safeguards, such as input validation, proper exception handling, and the use of secure serialization/deserialization frameworks or libraries, are in place to prevent serialization/deserialization attacks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.

entries.title: OS Command Injection Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that safe mechanisms, such as parameterized commands or libraries with built-in protection, are used to prevent command injection vulnerabilities. Assess whether user inputs are properly validated and sanitized before being used in command execution. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:

entries.title: HTML Output Encoding Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The JSP template contains a raw expression in a potentially rendered output position. Known JSTL control attributes and default escaping output are excluded; source provenance and output context require review.
entries.impact: If externally influenced text reaches browser output without the required context encoding, it may inject markup or script. A model value or expression alone does not establish attacker control.
entries.remediation:
Encode untrusted values for their HTML, attribute, URL or script context. Prefer escaping output helpers for HTML text, and validate URL destinations separately.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Trace the model or session value to its origin and identify the rendering context. Verify tag-library bindings and explicit escapeXml settings. Imported templates, custom tags and expression nesting require separate review.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: World-Writable Storage Review
entries.description: The source references a dependency, version, or deprecated API. Resolve the actual deployed version and supported behavior before deciding whether it needs replacement.
entries.impact: A reachable vulnerability in an unsupported or affected dependency may compromise the application with its privileges. A version declaration or deprecated API alone does not establish that such a vulnerability is present.
entries.remediation:
Inventory resolved dependencies and runtime versions, compare them with authoritative advisories and support policy, and migrate affected or unsupported components to tested supported replacements.

Recommended actions:
1. Replace unsupported APIs or affected dependencies with a supported option after checking application compatibility.
2. Pin and verify the deployed version and test the affected behavior and error paths after the update.
entries.reviewer:
Check Java/Kotlin source files for occurrences of MODE_WORLD_WRITEABLE and ensure that secure alternatives are used. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Resolve the dependency or deprecated API version actually included in the deployed artifact.
2. Inspect the affected functionality and its callers; a declaration or API name alone does not establish a reachable vulnerability.
3. Check supported replacements and compatibility requirements, and record evidence for any affected deployed behavior.

entries.title: File Path and Access Review
entries.description: The code accesses, creates, deletes, or shares filesystem data. Resolve path provenance, destination containment, permission modes, and any concurrent access.
entries.impact: An attacker controlling a path or shared file may read or replace private files, delete data, or redirect an operation outside its intended directory if containment and access controls are ineffective.
entries.remediation:
Resolve paths beneath a fixed permitted root and verify containment and effective permissions. Use safe exclusive temporary-file creation, restrict sharing, and account for symlinks and concurrent changes.

Recommended actions:
1. Resolve paths against a fixed permitted root and enforce containment with filesystem-aware checks; avoid simple prefix checks.
2. Use application-controlled file identifiers where possible, restrict filesystem privileges, and test traversal and archive extraction boundaries.
entries.reviewer:
Review Java/Kotlin source files for file operations that use insecure modes, ensuring that secure alternatives are implemented. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace external influence over the path and resolve it as the filesystem will, including relative segments and symbolic links.
2. Check the resolved destination remains within the permitted root and that the caller is authorized for the specific file operation.
3. Inspect read, write and extraction paths separately; record the effective path restrictions and deployment permissions.

entries.title: Outgoing URI Intent Review
entries.description: A constructed intent receives a URI. Resolve its actual scheme, destination handler, URI grants and sensitive content; an HTTP URL does not require a FileProvider.
entries.impact: An unintended recipient, untrusted URI scheme or overly broad content grant can expose data when a sensitive value reaches this outgoing intent. A VIEW intent alone does not prove nested-intent forwarding, incoming export or private-file disclosure.
entries.remediation:
Validate the scheme and intended recipient. Use a content provider with narrowly scoped grants when sharing private files; for remote URLs, protect transport and encode request components. An unrelated provider import or grant elsewhere does not protect this operation.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep internal components private where possible; enforce caller permissions and resource authorization on exposed operations.
2. Constrain recipients and granted access and test calls from an untrusted process or application.
entries.reviewer:
Trace the same URI into the launched intent and distinguish remote web links from private-file sharing. Review the selected handler, release reachability and data sensitivity before confirming exposure.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective export status, permission requirements and runtime identity checks on the inter-process interface.
2. Trace untrusted callers and received values to sensitive actions, including indirect recipients and granted resource access.
3. Verify unauthorized callers cannot invoke the protected operation; a declared component or intent alone is not an issue.

entries.title: File Upload Review
entries.description: The application accepts uploaded content. Identify storage destinations, execution behavior, filename handling, and the effective size and type checks.
entries.impact: A crafted upload may execute as application code, overwrite files, disclose data through later processing, or exhaust storage if the upload crosses the intended content and filesystem boundaries.
entries.remediation:
Allowlist required file types, inspect content rather than trusting extensions, bound sizes, generate server-side names, and store uploads outside executable paths with appropriate access controls.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply permitted type and size limits, use application-controlled storage names and keep uploaded content outside executable locations.
2. Authorize upload and retrieval independently and test disallowed content, oversized input and filename traversal.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that file uploads are properly validated and sanitized. Assess whether the necessary checks, such as file type and size validation, are in place. Also ensure that uploaded files are stored securely and that access controls are applied appropriately. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace who supplies the upload and inspect size limits, filename handling, storage destination and downstream processing.
2. Check whether uploaded content can execute, be rendered as active content or overwrite a protected file.
3. Inspect file-type checks and authorization to create and retrieve the content; record the reachable unsafe behavior.

entries.title: Request Dispatch Destination Review
entries.description: The code computes a request dispatch or redirect destination. Trace its origin and check which routes or external locations it may select.
entries.impact: Caller-controlled destinations may expose unintended handlers or redirect users to an attacker-selected location when effective route and destination controls are missing. This check does not establish local file inclusion.
entries.remediation:
Use fixed routes where possible. Validate computed destinations against permitted routes or local locations and enforce authorization on the destination handler.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer application route identifiers mapped to fixed destinations; permit only necessary relative paths or explicitly allowed external destinations.
2. Reject unsupported schemes and ambiguous destinations and test redirect handling after decoding and normalization.
entries.reviewer:
Trace computed dispatch and redirect destinations to their callers. Check permitted routes and local destination controls. A dispatch or redirect call alone does not establish file inclusion or an exploitable redirect.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether untrusted input controls the redirect destination and whether the redirect is reachable.
2. Inspect URL parsing, relative versus absolute destinations, scheme handling and authorization around the redirect.
3. Check how encoded or ambiguous URLs are interpreted by the framework and browser before confirming an unsafe redirect.

entries.title: Random Number Generation Review
entries.description: The checked source uses a random generator, cryptographic primitive, or initialization value whose suitability depends on its security purpose and inputs.
entries.impact: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.

Recommended actions:
1. Use maintained high-level cryptographic APIs appropriate to the purpose; use authenticated encryption for confidential application data.
2. For passwords, use the platform password-hashing facility rather than a fast general-purpose digest. Verify key, nonce and migration handling for affected data.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that the java.util.Random package is used appropriately and assess the security implications. Check whether the java.security.SecureRandom class is used where secure random values are required. Also evaluate the context in which the java.util.Random package is used and determine if there are any security risks associated with the predictable nature of its random number generation. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the purpose of the cryptographic operation, algorithm, mode, key or nonce handling, and protected data.
2. Distinguish password storage, confidentiality, integrity and non-security checksums; each requires different controls.
3. Inspect deployed configuration and all encrypt, decrypt or verification paths before deciding whether the use is unsafe.

entries.title: HTTP Client Usage Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Check for the proper usage of HTTP connections and verify that secure protocols (like HTTPS) are enforced for all communications. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: Collection Library Usage Review
entries.description: The application reads serialized objects or uses a parser that may construct runtime types. Identify the input’s trust and the effective parser and type restrictions.
entries.impact: A crafted untrusted payload may instantiate dangerous types or trigger object behavior that executes code, modifies state, or exhausts resources when the parser permits those operations.
entries.remediation:
Use a data-only format and a safe loader for untrusted input. Disable automatic object or type construction, allowlist required types, and bound parsing size and complexity.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer a data-only format mapped to explicit application types; avoid reconstructing arbitrary runtime objects from untrusted input.
2. Restrict allowed types and converters, limit input size and nesting, and test rejection of unexpected type metadata.
entries.reviewer:
Evaluate the use of the Apache Commons Collections library and assess whether it is being used securely and with proper data validation. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the serializer, accepted data format and whether external input controls type selection or object construction.
2. Inspect allowed types, converters, polymorphic handling and object hooks; distinguish ordinary data parsing from unsafe object reconstruction.
3. Verify reachable callers, integrity checks and failure paths before treating deserialization as exploitable.

entries.title: XML Parser Configuration Review
entries.description: The code parses or transforms XML. Resolve external entity, DTD, and resource-loading settings for the actual parser instance.
entries.impact: If external resources or entity expansion are permitted for untrusted XML, an attacker may read local files, make requests to internal services, or exhaust parser resources.
entries.remediation:
Disable external entities and DTD loading for untrusted XML, use a restrictive resolver, and enforce input-size and expansion limits on the effective parser.

Recommended actions:
1. Configure the parser to disable unneeded external entities and DTD processing; restrict resolvers when those features are necessary.
2. Apply document and expansion limits and test prohibited file or network resolution in the deployed parser configuration.
entries.reviewer:
Ensure that the XML parsing is done securely, with proper configurations in place to mitigate XXE vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the parser and whether untrusted XML reaches it; inspect its effective settings rather than relying on library defaults.
2. Check external entity resolution, DTD processing, network or file access, and limits for document size and expansion.
3. Inspect all parser construction paths and error handling; record which reachable path lacks the required restrictions.

entries.title: Session Cookie Protection Review
entries.description: The code handles session state or configures cookies and session secrets. Resolve cookie attributes, token generation, lifetime, and server-side validation.
entries.impact: Weak session secrets, exposed cookies, or inadequate expiry may allow session theft, token forgery, or continued access after the user’s intended authorization ends.
entries.remediation:
Use strong unpredictable session secrets, rotate tokens on privilege changes, and enforce expiry and revocation. Set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite attributes for sensitive browser cookies.

Recommended actions:
1. Set cookie protections appropriate to its purpose and deployed HTTPS flow; keep sensitive session cookies inaccessible to scripts where required.
2. Limit cookie scope and lifetime, rotate sessions at authentication changes, and test actual browser and response-header behavior.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that the 'httpOnly' flag is properly set for cookies handling sensitive information or participating in session management. Check whether the 'httpOnly' attribute is included in the Set-Cookie header for relevant cookies. Also assess the impact of missing 'httpOnly' flags and confirm that the necessary security measures are in place to prevent client-side attacks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify whether the cookie carries a session or other sensitive value and inspect the flags on every issuance and update path.
2. Check effective Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite behavior, domain and path scope, expiry and session rotation in the deployed flow.
3. Distinguish intended browser access from a missing protection; verify actual response headers and cross-site behavior.

entries.title: CSRF Protection Review
entries.description: The code disables, exempts, or configures request-forgery protection. Verify whether a reachable state-changing operation authenticates through automatically sent browser credentials.
entries.impact: An attacker may cause a victim’s browser to perform unwanted authenticated actions if the endpoint relies on ambient credentials and lacks an effective anti-forgery check.
entries.remediation:
Enforce anti-forgery protection on cookie-authenticated state changes, validate origins where appropriate, and justify exemptions only for independently authenticated non-browser flows.

Recommended actions:
1. Enforce the framework anti-forgery mechanism on state-changing browser-authenticated requests; keep exemptions narrow and documented.
2. Use appropriate cookie and origin protections as additional controls and test rejected cross-site requests.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that CSRF protection mechanisms are properly implemented and enabled for all relevant requests. Check for any instances where CSRF protection is explicitly disabled and assess the impact of such configurations. Also evaluate the effectiveness of the implemented CSRF protection measures in preventing CSRF attacks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify whether the reachable endpoint changes state and whether browsers attach authentication credentials automatically.
2. Inspect the effective anti-forgery check, accepted methods and content types, origin checks and intentional exemptions.
3. Test a cross-site request against the deployed authentication flow; distinguish token-based APIs from cookie-authenticated operations.

entries.title: Disabled Input Validation
entries.description: The code accepts or reads externally influenced data. Trace it to security-sensitive operations and identify the validation and authorization required by each destination.
entries.impact: External input may cause injection, incorrect decisions, or unauthorized data access if it reaches a sensitive operation without the controls required by that operation. Reading input alone does not establish a vulnerability.
entries.remediation:
Validate type, size, and allowed values at trust boundaries, and apply destination-specific parameter binding or output encoding. Enforce authorization independently of input validation.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that input validation mechanisms are properly implemented and enabled for all relevant data inputs. Identify any instances where input validation is explicitly disabled and assess the impact of such configurations. Also evaluate the effectiveness of the implemented input validation measures in preventing common security vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Application Logging Review
entries.description: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Log only the operational details needed, redact sensitive values, and return limited error messages to clients.
2. Restrict diagnostic and log access and test production error responses and representative log output.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that the usage of logger functions (error, warn, info, debug, trace) in Java code is appropriate and adheres to secure coding practices. Assess whether proper validation mechanisms are in place to prevent the logging of sensitive information. Also review the log configurations to ensure that log levels are set appropriately and sensitive data is not leaked through the logs. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched path logs sensitive data or exposes diagnostics to an untrusted recipient.
2. Trace the actual values, redaction and error handling, including production configuration and log retention or access.
3. Distinguish internal operational diagnostics from client-visible output and record the reachable disclosure path without reproducing secrets.

entries.title: Cleartext HTTP Communication Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that sensitive data is not transmitted over unencrypted HTTP connections. Assess whether appropriate encryption mechanisms are implemented using HTTP client classes and ensure the proper validation of server certificates. Also evaluate the overall security architecture and ensure that secure communication practices are followed. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: Sensitive Data Logging Review
entries.description: A console or logger call emits an identifier associated with credential or authentication material. Literal message labels alone are excluded. Resolve the value and log audience.
entries.impact: Log readers may recover passwords, active authentication tokens or one-time codes when those values are emitted without redaction. A variable name does not prove the value is an active credential.
entries.remediation:
Remove credential values from diagnostics. Log event identifiers and non-sensitive metadata, and redact sensitive fields before they reach a logging sink.

Recommended actions:
1. Log only the operational details needed, redact sensitive values, and return limited error messages to clients.
2. Restrict diagnostic and log access and test production error responses and representative log output.
entries.reviewer:
Check the emitted value, masking or hashing, production reachability, retention and access controls. Custom logging wrappers and unresolved argument expressions require separate review.

3. Distinguish internal operational diagnostics from client-visible output and record the reachable disclosure path without reproducing secrets.

entries.title: SQL Query Construction Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Check if parameterized queries with `PreparedStatement` are used for SELECT statements with WHERE or ORDER BY clauses to prevent SQL injection risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: XML External Entity Review
entries.description: The code parses or transforms XML. Resolve external entity, DTD, and resource-loading settings for the actual parser instance.
entries.impact: If external resources or entity expansion are permitted for untrusted XML, an attacker may read local files, make requests to internal services, or exhaust parser resources.
entries.remediation:
Disable external entities and DTD loading for untrusted XML, use a restrictive resolver, and enforce input-size and expansion limits on the effective parser.

Recommended actions:
1. Configure the parser to disable unneeded external entities and DTD processing; restrict resolvers when those features are necessary.
2. Apply document and expansion limits and test prohibited file or network resolution in the deployed parser configuration.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that all XML parser instantiations are followed by feature disablement for external entities and DTDs. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the parser and whether untrusted XML reaches it; inspect its effective settings rather than relying on library defaults.
2. Check external entity resolution, DTD processing, network or file access, and limits for document size and expansion.
3. Inspect all parser construction paths and error handling; record which reachable path lacks the required restrictions.

entries.title: LDAP Injection Review
entries.description: The code constructs a directory query, XPath expression, or naming-service lookup. Review which input controls query syntax or the lookup target.
entries.impact: Attacker-controlled query syntax may bypass intended selection or authorization and expose protected records. An attacker-selected naming-service target may also invoke unsafe remote resolution, depending on runtime behavior.
entries.remediation:
Keep untrusted values out of expression structure and remote naming targets. Use context-appropriate parameter binding or escaping, fixed trusted lookup destinations, and least-privileged service credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Use the query API’s parameter mechanism or syntax-specific escaping for data values; restrict externally selected lookup destinations.
2. Test that unusual input cannot alter query structure or bypass access controls; avoid substituting generic sanitization for the required control.
entries.reviewer:
Trace user input flow into LDAP filter construction and verify proper escaping at every injection point. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect how untrusted values enter the directory query, selection expression or naming-service lookup.
2. Distinguish data parameters from syntax and determine whether external input can alter the selected records or remote target.
3. Verify the exact API-specific escaping, binding or destination restrictions and resource authorization at the use point.

entries.title: Explicit Anonymous Operation Review
entries.description: An explicit anonymous-access declaration is present. Associate it with the affected route and operations, including inherited policy requirements.
entries.impact: Public access is often intentional. A defect exists only if the reachable operation requires identity or resource permissions that are not enforced.
entries.remediation:
Declare public entry points intentionally and enforce the required resource permissions at sensitive operations. Test neighboring protected routes and override behavior.

Recommended actions:

1. Use exact approved origins and verify credentialed preflight and actual responses. Authentication and authorization remain independent controls.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:

2. Check the control on the actual path; unrelated markers must not suppress the candidate.
3. Validate a reachable unsafe case and a protected control before confirming the issue.

entries.title: Tenant Data Constraint Review
entries.description: A tenant or organization identifier is associated with a data operation. Verify its provenance and application-specific isolation invariant.
entries.impact: Caller-selected tenant identity or an incomplete constraint may expose another tenant's records. Marker presence and absence do not establish isolation.
entries.remediation:
Derive the effective tenant from trusted authenticated context, apply it to the exact data operation and verify access using two distinct tenants.

Recommended actions:
1. Derive the effective tenant from trusted authenticated context, apply it to the exact data operation and verify access using two distinct tenants.

2. Check the control on the actual path; unrelated markers must not suppress the candidate.
3. Validate a reachable unsafe case and a protected control before confirming the issue.

entries.title: Untrusted Input Entry Point
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code accepts or reads externally influenced data. Trace it to security-sensitive operations and identify the validation and authorization required by each destination.
entries.impact: External input may cause injection, incorrect decisions, or unauthorized data access if it reaches a sensitive operation without the controls required by that operation. Reading input alone does not establish a vulnerability.
entries.remediation:
Validate type, size, and allowed values at trust boundaries, and apply destination-specific parameter binding or output encoding. Enforce authorization independently of input validation.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Ensure that proper input handling is in place for user input obtained through `document. getElementById(). value`. Verify that developers have implemented appropriate input validation and sanitization techniques to prevent security vulnerabilities related to unvalidated input. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: HTML Output Encoding Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: A value is assigned to innerHTML. The browser parses this value as HTML; the assignment alone does not establish attacker control.
entries.impact: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
entries.remediation:
Use textContent for text. If HTML is required, sanitize it with a maintained HTML allowlist sanitizer immediately before insertion. Review Trusted Types policies for unsafe pass-through behavior.

Recommended actions:
1. Use textContent or createElement for ordinary content.
2. Sanitize deliberately accepted HTML at its insertion boundary; input validation or CSP alone is not output encoding.
entries.reviewer:
Trace the assigned expression to URL data, messages, form values, storage and server responses. Check whether executable markup survives sanitization in the actual element context. Fixed markup and correctly sanitized content do not establish cross-site scripting.

Review steps:
1. Follow every value used to build the innerHTML assignment.
2. Inspect sanitization and any transformations after it.
3. Verify a reachable input-to-HTML path under the effective browser policy.

entries.title: HTML Output Encoding Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: document.write passes content to the document parser. Review each dynamic fragment and its rendering context.
entries.impact: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
entries.remediation:
Replace document.write with DOM construction and textContent for text. Keep external values out of script and event-handler syntax; sanitize deliberately accepted HTML at the insertion boundary.

Recommended actions:
1. Construct elements explicitly and set text properties.
2. Remove string-built scripts and event handlers; HTML sanitization does not make arbitrary JavaScript strings safe.
entries.reviewer:
Trace each document.write argument, decoding step and concatenated fragment. Determine whether an attacker can introduce executable markup in the actual parser context and document lifecycle. Fixed application markup is not a confirmed vulnerability.

Review steps:
1. Identify dynamic fragments in document.write arguments.
2. Trace their origin, decoding and sanitization.
3. Verify the parser context and a reachable payload that bypasses the relevant protection.

entries.title: HTML Output Encoding Review
entries.description: Application data is inserted into an HTML or script rendering context, or marked safe in a way that may bypass automatic encoding.
entries.impact: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
entries.remediation:

2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
