3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: OS Command Injection Review
entries.description: The code invokes a process or shell execution API. Trace the executable, arguments, shell use, and source of externally supplied values.
entries.impact: If attacker-controlled data changes command syntax or executable selection, an attacker may execute commands with application privileges, read or modify files, or disrupt service.
entries.remediation:
Use a fixed executable with a separate argument array and avoid a shell where possible. Validate arguments for the selected program and allowlist permitted operations.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer a library API or a fixed executable with a separate argument array; avoid passing external text to a shell.
2. Restrict permitted operations and arguments, constrain option handling, and test rejected input under the actual deployment privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Verify whether the code implements sufficient measures to prevent remote OS command execution vulnerabilities. Check whether the usage of `child_process. exec()` is necessary, and if so, ensure that proper input validation, sanitization, and command parameterization techniques are implemented to prevent command injection attacks. Also assess the context in which this function is used and verify that security best practices are followed to mitigate any potential risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the executable, arguments, shell use and working directory; trace external influence over each.
2. Check whether a shell interprets metacharacters or whether options can change command behavior even without a shell.
3. Verify the operation is reachable and examine validation, executable selection and process privileges before confirming an issue.

entries.title: Dynamic Code Evaluation Review
entries.description: The code calls eval or a timer API. eval interprets code; setTimeout and setInterval evaluate code only when the callback argument is a string.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace dynamic evaluation with fixed operations and data-only parsing. Pass function callbacks to setTimeout and setInterval and keep external values out of executable strings.

Recommended actions:
1. Use function callbacks for timers.
2. Use JSON.parse for JSON data and fixed dispatch tables for permitted operations.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect the actual argument type. A function callback passed to a timer is not string evaluation. For eval or a string callback, trace who controls the executed text and verify the reachable browser or server context.

Review steps:
1. Distinguish eval from timer calls.
2. Determine whether a timer callback is a function or a string.
3. Trace control over interpreted text and the privileges of execution.

entries.title: Weak Cryptographic Operation Review
entries.description: The checked source uses a random generator, cryptographic primitive, or initialization value whose suitability depends on its security purpose and inputs.
entries.impact: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.

Recommended actions:
1. Use maintained high-level cryptographic APIs appropriate to the purpose; use authenticated encryption for confidential application data.
2. For passwords, use the platform password-hashing facility rather than a fast general-purpose digest. Verify key, nonce and migration handling for affected data.
entries.reviewer:
Weak cryptographic functions are used in the code. Assess whether the code uses secure cryptographic algorithms and if best practices for encryption and hashing are followed. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the purpose of the cryptographic operation, algorithm, mode, key or nonce handling, and protected data.
2. Distinguish password storage, confidentiality, integrity and non-security checksums; each requires different controls.
3. Inspect deployed configuration and all encrypt, decrypt or verification paths before deciding whether the use is unsafe.

entries.title: Random Number Generation Review
entries.description: A general-purpose random generator is used. Trace its value to a security-sensitive consumer before confirming weak token, nonce or credential generation.
entries.impact: Predictable secrets or unsuitable cryptographic parameters may enable credential guessing, reveal plaintext, or weaken integrity when used to protect security-sensitive data. Non-security hashes and identifiers do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Use a cryptographically secure generator for secrets and modern purpose-appropriate cryptography. Use unique nonces, protected keys, and a vetted password-hashing scheme where passwords are stored.

Recommended actions:
1. Use maintained high-level cryptographic APIs appropriate to the purpose; use authenticated encryption for confidential application data.
2. For passwords, use the platform password-hashing facility rather than a fast general-purpose digest. Verify key, nonce and migration handling for affected data.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that Math.random() is not used where cryptographic randomness is required. Confirm that security-sensitive identifiers use a CSPRNG. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the purpose of the cryptographic operation, algorithm, mode, key or nonce handling, and protected data.
2. Distinguish password storage, confidentiality, integrity and non-security checksums; each requires different controls.
3. Inspect deployed configuration and all encrypt, decrypt or verification paths before deciding whether the use is unsafe.

entries.title: Routes
entries.description: The code declares an entry point, model, destination, or configuration value that may cross a trust boundary. Identify callers, recipients, and the required data-access policy.
entries.impact: A boundary that trusts unauthorized callers or exposes private output may permit data disclosure or state changes. A declaration, address, or architectural marker alone does not establish such a failure.
entries.remediation:
Trace the actual boundary, restrict accepted inputs and recipients, and enforce authentication and object-level authorization where required. Verify both authorized and denied use cases.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.
2. Add a regression case for the unsafe condition and a valid protected case; verify the effective behavior in the relevant deployment.
entries.reviewer:
Verify whether the code contains hardcoded routes and assess the potential security implications. Ensure that sensitive information, such as internal URLs, API endpoints, or authentication routes, is not exposed through hardcoded routes. Also check if the code implements appropriate access control measures and adheres to secure coding practices, such as using configuration files or dynamic routing mechanisms. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched construct in its containing function or configuration and identify the security-sensitive behavior under review.
2. Verify reachable callers, external influence and effective protections, including deployment overrides and failure paths.
3. Record concrete evidence for a confirmed issue or a justified suppression; retain an unresolved outcome when the required evidence is unavailable.

entries.title: Error Detail Disclosure Review
entries.description: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Log only the operational details needed, redact sensitive values, and return limited error messages to clients.
2. Restrict diagnostic and log access and test production error responses and representative log output.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm that HTTP responses never include raw error objects, stack traces, or internal diagnostic details. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched path logs sensitive data or exposes diagnostics to an untrusted recipient.
2. Trace the actual values, redaction and error handling, including production configuration and log retention or access.
3. Distinguish internal operational diagnostics from client-visible output and record the reachable disclosure path without reproducing secrets.

entries.title: Node Inspector Exposure Review
entries.description: A configuration or API enables development diagnostics, process inspection, or debugging. Verify whether it applies to a deployed production artifact.
entries.impact: An actor with access to an enabled debugging interface may inspect private state or influence application execution; exposed development endpoints may disclose internal implementation details.
entries.remediation:
Disable debugging and development endpoints in production, bind necessary diagnostic services to restricted interfaces, and verify the final deployed artifact and access policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Disable development-only functionality in production and enforce the environment boundary in deployment configuration.
2. Restrict operational diagnostics and add a production-configuration check covering the exposed route or feature.
entries.reviewer:
Verify runtime scripts and deployment manifests do not expose inspector endpoints in production environments. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective production configuration and determine who can reach debugging or development functionality.
2. Check environment guards, deployment overrides and the information or capabilities exposed by the feature.
3. Verify the actual production behavior; a development-only setting is not itself a production vulnerability.

entries.title: Permissive HTTP Parser Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm parser hardening remains enabled across app servers and reverse-proxy boundaries. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.

entries.title: Security Control Bypass Review
entries.description: The code contains a security-control marker. Its presence is a review surface rather than evidence that the control is defective or consistently enforced.
entries.impact: No adverse security consequence follows from the presence of a protection alone. If it is bypassed or applied outside the correct context, the protected operation may still permit injection or unauthorized access.
entries.remediation:
Verify that the control applies to every relevant entry point and uses the required context and policy. Retain effective protections; test bypass cases before recommending a change.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.
2. Add a regression case for the unsafe condition and a valid protected case; verify the effective behavior in the relevant deployment.
entries.reviewer:
Identify weak or inadequate security mitigations in the code and recommend implementing stronger security measures. Assess whether the application applies appropriate security controls and avoids relying on weak mitigations that may be easily bypassed by attackers. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched construct in its containing function or configuration and identify the security-sensitive behavior under review.
2. Verify reachable callers, external influence and effective protections, including deployment overrides and failure paths.
3. Record concrete evidence for a confirmed issue or a justified suppression; retain an unresolved outcome when the required evidence is unavailable.

entries.title: SQL Query Construction Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.
entries.remediation:
Bind data values as parameters, choose dynamic identifiers from a fixed allowlist, and enforce object-level access checks. Trace the complete query construction before replacing a safe query.

Recommended actions:
1. Bind data values with the driver or ORM parameter API; avoid constructing query syntax from external strings.
2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:
Check if parameterized queries or query bindings are used with SELECT statements containing WHERE or ORDER BY clauses in JavaScript applications to ensure secure handling of user input. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: JavaScript Legacy API Review
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

Recommended actions:

2. Keep template or expression sources under application control; restrict exposed capabilities and test rejection of unexpected syntax.
entries.reviewer:
Check for the usage of deprecated JavaScript functions and recommend replacing them with safer alternatives. Assess whether the codebase follows best practices and avoids deprecated functions that may pose security risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

entries.title: Object Authorization Review
entries.description: The checked code implements an identity, access-control, or abuse-prevention decision. Determine the trusted verifier, protected resources, and whether the control is enforced on every relevant path.
entries.impact: If identity or resource authorization can be bypassed, an attacker may impersonate a user, access another user’s data, or perform restricted operations. A control’s presence alone does not establish a weakness.
entries.remediation:
Enforce authentication and object-level authorization on the trusted server or privileged boundary. Use strong verifier material, appropriate rate limits and recovery controls, and test access by unauthenticated and insufficiently privileged callers.

Recommended actions:
1. Enforce authorization on the server for each protected action and resource; deny requests without an explicit permitted outcome.
2. Add tests for cross-user and cross-tenant access and ensure alternate routes cannot bypass the same policy.
entries.reviewer:
Verify whether the code implements proper authorization and access control mechanisms to prevent IDOR vulnerabilities. Check whether user input used to access resources is properly validated, sanitized, and authorized. Reviewers should assess the effectiveness of the implemented measures in mitigating IDOR risks. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify the actor, action and protected resource, including ownership and tenant boundaries.
2. Trace every reachable request or service path and inspect the effective permission check before sensitive work occurs.
3. Test unauthenticated access, insufficient roles and access to another user or tenant; record effective middleware and service-level controls.

entries.title: Outbound Request Destination Review
entries.description: An outbound request operation is present. Resolve client versus server runtime, destination authority, redirects and attacker influence before classifying SSRF. A fixed-authority mobile client request alone is not SSRF.
entries.impact: If an attacker can select a reachable destination, the application may expose internal services or metadata credentials, or send protected data to an unauthorized recipient.
entries.remediation:
Allowlist required destinations and protocols, validate resolved addresses and every redirect, and restrict outbound access to internal and metadata services.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer fixed destinations or a restricted set of permitted services; validate schemes, hosts and ports before the request.
2. Apply destination checks to redirects and resolved addresses where applicable, restrict network egress, and test prohibited destinations.
entries.reviewer:
XMLHttpRequest, fetch, axios, http. request, https. request, http. get, https. get, http. post, https. post, http. put, https. put, http. delete, https. delete, or $. ajax functions are used with potentially untrusted URLs. Assess whether proper input validation and URL restriction mechanisms are implemented to mitigate SSRF vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Verify the operation makes a server-side request, then trace external control over the URL, host, port and redirects.
2. Inspect destination restrictions, DNS resolution and redirect handling; distinguish fixed destinations from caller-controlled requests.
3. Check deployment egress controls and whether internal services or local files are reachable from the requesting process.

entries.title: Prototype Pollution
entries.description: The code writes object properties or merges data in a way that may affect prototype state. Determine whether externally supplied keys can reach the operation.
entries.impact: An attacker who changes shared prototype properties may alter authorization decisions or other application behavior; some reachable gadgets may also lead to data disclosure or code execution.
entries.remediation:
Reject prototype-manipulating keys such as __proto__, constructor, and prototype where appropriate. Use safe own-property handling, null-prototype dictionaries, and maintained merge libraries.

Recommended actions:
1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.
2. Add a regression case for the unsafe condition and a valid protected case; verify the effective behavior in the relevant deployment.
entries.reviewer:
The code directly uses or modifies the `__proto__` property or assigns values to properties of `Object. prototype` (excluding `hasOwnProperty`). Assess whether proper precautions are taken to prevent prototype pollution vulnerabilities. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the matched construct in its containing function or configuration and identify the security-sensitive behavior under review.
2. Verify reachable callers, external influence and effective protections, including deployment overrides and failure paths.
3. Record concrete evidence for a confirmed issue or a justified suppression; retain an unresolved outcome when the required evidence is unavailable.

entries.title: Session Cookie Protection Review
entries.description: The code handles session state or configures cookies and session secrets. Resolve cookie attributes, token generation, lifetime, and server-side validation.
entries.impact: Weak session secrets, exposed cookies, or inadequate expiry may allow session theft, token forgery, or continued access after the user’s intended authorization ends.
entries.remediation:
Use strong unpredictable session secrets, rotate tokens on privilege changes, and enforce expiry and revocation. Set Secure, HttpOnly, and appropriate SameSite attributes for sensitive browser cookies.

Recommended actions:
1. Set cookie protections appropriate to its purpose and deployed HTTPS flow; keep sensitive session cookies inaccessible to scripts where required.
2. Limit cookie scope and lifetime, rotate sessions at authentication changes, and test actual browser and response-header behavior.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm that all cookies setting session or authentication state include httpOnly, secure, and sameSite attributes. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify whether the cookie carries a session or other sensitive value and inspect the flags on every issuance and update path.
2. Check effective Secure, HttpOnly and SameSite behavior, domain and path scope, expiry and session rotation in the deployed flow.
3. Distinguish intended browser access from a missing protection; verify actual response headers and cross-site behavior.

entries.title: Bulk Object Field Binding Review
entries.description: An operation copies or binds object fields in bulk. Review the exact source, destination type and writable fields; this candidate does not establish mass assignment.
entries.impact: If untrusted fields can set privilege, ownership or protected state, a caller may exceed the intended operation permissions.
entries.remediation:
Use an explicit request schema and an operation-specific writable-field allowlist. Assign ownership, tenant and privilege fields from trusted server context.

Recommended actions:

entries.title: Untrusted Input Entry Point
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code accepts or reads externally influenced data. Trace it to security-sensitive operations and identify the validation and authorization required by each destination.
entries.impact: External input may cause injection, incorrect decisions, or unauthorized data access if it reaches a sensitive operation without the controls required by that operation. Reading input alone does not establish a vulnerability.
entries.remediation:
Validate type, size, and allowed values at trust boundaries, and apply destination-specific parameter binding or output encoding. Enforce authorization independently of input validation.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Ensure that proper input handling is in place for Intent extras. Verify that developers have implemented appropriate input validation and sanitization techniques to prevent security vulnerabilities related to untrusted inputs. Also assess the sensitivity of the data handled through Intent extras and confirm that relevant security measures, such as output encoding and protection against injection attacks, are implemented correctly. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.description: The code invokes a process or shell execution API. Trace the executable, arguments, shell use, and source of externally supplied values.
entries.impact: If attacker-controlled data changes command syntax or executable selection, an attacker may execute commands with application privileges, read or modify files, or disrupt service.

entries.reviewer:

2. Inspect navigation, message validation and resource or operation authorization on the native side.

entries.title: Content Provider Query Review
entries.description: The code constructs a query, selection, or ordering clause with values that may be externally controlled. Resolve whether those values enter syntax or bound data.
entries.impact: Attacker-controlled query syntax may change selected records, bypass intended filters, or modify stored data with the connection or provider’s privileges.
entries.remediation:

Recommended actions:

2. Use fixed mappings for dynamic identifiers and ordering. Test that unusual input remains data and that the database account has only required privileges.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Locate the final query and determine whether caller-controlled data can alter its structure; inspect interpolated fragments and raw-query helpers.
2. Verify that values are bound by the database driver. For identifiers or sort directions that cannot be bound, inspect a fixed mapping of allowed choices.
3. Record the reachable caller and effective controls; a constant query or correctly bound value does not establish injection.

entries.title: Shared Preferences Usage Review
entries.description: The application stores sensitive values or configures protection for persistent data. Determine the actual storage location, backup policy, and lock-state access restrictions.
entries.impact: An actor with access to unprotected application files, backups, or overly broad keychain access may recover credentials or private records and use them outside the intended trust boundary.

2. Inspect encryption, key access and data retention, including copies in caches, backups and exported artifacts.
3. Verify access under the relevant attacker model; a storage API alone does not establish an exposure.

entries.title: Coroutine Failure Handling Review
entries.description: The code configures failure handling or resource consumption. Determine whether failure paths preserve security invariants and whether work is bounded.
entries.impact: Unhandled failures or unbounded work may disrupt availability or leave security-relevant state inconsistent. The presence or absence of a named handler alone does not establish a reachable security defect.
entries.remediation:
Bound resource use, handle failures at the correct ownership boundary, and fail safely before updating trusted state. Test exceptional paths, cancellation, timeouts, and recovery behavior.

Recommended actions:
1. Set limits and timeouts appropriate to the operation and release resources on success, failure and cancellation.
2. Test oversized input and concurrent requests against the intended limits and verify cleanup under failure.
entries.reviewer:
Verify that coroutines performing security-sensitive operations (queries, crypto, auth) have explicit error handling and do not silently discard exceptions. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace who controls the operation count, input size, duration or resource allocation.
2. Inspect limits, cancellation, cleanup and error paths, including concurrency and deployment quotas.
3. Establish a reachable way to exhaust or retain a relevant resource before confirming an availability issue.

Recommended actions:

2. If rich HTML is required, use a maintained sanitizer with a restricted policy; validate URL schemes and test the actual browser output.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Trace the matched value to its browser rendering context: text, attribute, URL, script or DOM operation.
2. Inspect the exact encoder or safe rendering API and any bypass of automatic escaping; verify it protects that context.

entries.description: The source references a dependency, version, or deprecated API. Resolve the actual deployed version and supported behavior before deciding whether it needs replacement.
entries.impact: A reachable vulnerability in an unsupported or affected dependency may compromise the application with its privileges. A version declaration or deprecated API alone does not establish that such a vulnerability is present.

Inventory resolved dependencies and runtime versions, compare them with authoritative advisories and support policy, and migrate affected or unsupported components to tested supported replacements.

2. Pin and verify the deployed version and test the affected behavior and error paths after the update.

2. Inspect the affected functionality and its callers; a declaration or API name alone does not establish a reachable vulnerability.

entries.title: File Path and Access Review
entries.description: The code accesses, creates, deletes, or shares filesystem data. Resolve path provenance, destination containment, permission modes, and any concurrent access.
entries.impact: An attacker controlling a path or shared file may read or replace private files, delete data, or redirect an operation outside its intended directory if containment and access controls are ineffective.
entries.remediation:
Resolve paths beneath a fixed permitted root and verify containment and effective permissions. Use safe exclusive temporary-file creation, restrict sharing, and account for symlinks and concurrent changes.

Recommended actions:
1. Resolve paths against a fixed permitted root and enforce containment with filesystem-aware checks; avoid simple prefix checks.
2. Use application-controlled file identifiers where possible, restrict filesystem privileges, and test traversal and archive extraction boundaries.
entries.reviewer:
Review Java/Kotlin source files for file operations that use insecure modes, ensuring that secure alternatives are implemented. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace external influence over the path and resolve it as the filesystem will, including relative segments and symbolic links.
2. Check the resolved destination remains within the permitted root and that the caller is authorized for the specific file operation.
3. Inspect read, write and extraction paths separately; record the effective path restrictions and deployment permissions.

entries.description: Review target: Content Providers with No Permissions. The application exposes or invokes an inter-process interface. entries.title: Static IV Review
entries.description: Review target: Hardcoded Static Initialization Vector. The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether the operation protects secrets, authenticates data or serves a non-security purpose; resolve algorithm, mode and key provenance.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials. Use supported authenticated cryptography, securely generated keys and nonces, and platform-backed key storage; replace hardcoded or constant key material.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
3. Use supported authenticated cryptography, securely generated keys and nonces, and platform-backed key storage; replace hardcoded or constant key material.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.

entries.remediation:

Recommended actions:
1. Use maintained high-level cryptographic APIs appropriate to the purpose; use authenticated encryption for confidential application data.
2. For passwords, use the platform password-hashing facility rather than a fast general-purpose digest. Verify key, nonce and migration handling for affected data.
3. Use supported authenticated cryptography, securely generated keys and nonces, and platform-backed key storage; replace hardcoded or constant key material.

Review steps:

4. Determine whether the operation protects secrets, authenticates data or serves a non-security purpose; resolve algorithm, mode and key provenance.

entries.title: External File Storage Review

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: Review target: Bad Certificate Callback Accepting All Certificates. The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs. Resolve the particular connection, host and client configuration selected by the shipped build.
entries.impact: An attacker on the network may read or alter affected traffic if sensitive data travels over cleartext or the connection accepts an untrusted server. Normal HTTPS endpoints and correctly implemented validation do not establish exposure.
entries.remediation:
Use HTTPS with normal certificate-chain and hostname verification. Remove permissive production callbacks and broad transport exceptions; restrict any justified exception to a documented, non-sensitive endpoint. Use platform trust and hostname validation and encrypted transport. Remove permissive callbacks and narrow necessary exceptions to the intended hosts.

Recommended actions:
1. Use authenticated encrypted transport and retain certificate and hostname verification; limit any development exception to a verified non-production scope.
2. Configure trust through the platform trust mechanism and test that invalid certificates and insecure protocol downgrades are rejected.
3. Use platform trust and hostname validation and encrypted transport. Remove permissive callbacks and narrow necessary exceptions to the intended hosts.
entries.reviewer:
Any unconditional true return in badCertificateCallback is a critical finding. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent. Test invalid chains, wrong hostnames, redirects and build-specific exceptions; an unrelated trusted client or HTTPS URL does not protect this connection. Missing pinning alone is not proof of insecurity.

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective connection settings, certificate-chain validation and hostname verification for the deployed client or server.
2. Trace configuration overrides, custom trust handlers and error paths; determine whether untrusted networks can affect the connection.
3. Verify the actual handshake and failure behavior against an untrusted or mismatched certificate before confirming a transport issue.
4. Resolve the particular connection, host and client configuration selected by the shipped build.
5. Test invalid chains, wrong hostnames, redirects and build-specific exceptions; an unrelated trusted client or HTTPS URL does not protect this connection. Missing pinning alone is not proof of insecurity.
6. Confirm reachability, the selected release build and the effect on a sensitive value before confirming an issue.

entries.title: HTTP Body Logging Review
entries.description: Review target: LogInterceptor with Response Body in Non-Debug Build. The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.

Recommended actions:
1. Log only the operational details needed, redact sensitive values, and return limited error messages to clients.
2. Restrict diagnostic and log access and test production error responses and representative log output.
3. Minimize collection and retention, redact secret values, and apply the platform controls needed for sensitive UI and data sharing.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm LogInterceptor with body logging is restricted to debug builds. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent. Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched path logs sensitive data or exposes diagnostics to an untrusted recipient.
2. Trace the actual values, redaction and error handling, including production configuration and log retention or access.
3. Distinguish internal operational diagnostics from client-visible output and record the reachable disclosure path without reproducing secrets.
4. Identify the actual sensitive value and the recipients, retention and user-consent context of this exposure or capability.
5. Test release logging, crash-report payloads, screenshot/background snapshots and clipboard lifetime; permission or API capability alone does not establish collection or malicious behavior.
6. Confirm reachability, the selected release build and the effect on a sensitive value before confirming an issue.

entries.title: Dio BaseOptions without Connection Timeout
entries.description: Review target: Dio BaseOptions Without Connection Timeout. The code configures failure handling or resource consumption. Determine whether failure paths preserve security invariants and whether work is bounded. Resolve the exact declaration or operation in the selected build and identify its security boundary.
entries.impact: Unhandled failures or unbounded work may disrupt availability or leave security-relevant state inconsistent. The presence or absence of a named handler alone does not establish a reachable security defect.
entries.remediation:
Bound resource use, handle failures at the correct ownership boundary, and fail safely before updating trusted state. Test exceptional paths, cancellation, timeouts, and recovery behavior. Apply the least-privilege platform control appropriate to the matched operation and verify the production configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Set limits and timeouts appropriate to the operation and release resources on success, failure and cancellation.
2. Test oversized input and concurrent requests against the intended limits and verify cleanup under failure.
3. Apply the least-privilege platform control appropriate to the matched operation and verify the production configuration.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm all Dio instances have timeouts configured. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent. Check debug/release and product flavors, generated/native code, plugin boundaries and failure paths; source evidence alone does not establish shipped or runtime behavior.

Review steps:
1. Trace who controls the operation count, input size, duration or resource allocation.
2. Inspect limits, cancellation, cleanup and error paths, including concurrency and deployment quotas.
3. Establish a reachable way to exhaust or retain a relevant resource before confirming an availability issue.
4. Resolve the exact declaration or operation in the selected build and identify its security boundary.
5. Check debug/release and product flavors, generated/native code, plugin boundaries and failure paths; source evidence alone does not establish shipped or runtime behavior.
6. Confirm reachability, the selected release build and the effect on a sensitive value before confirming an issue.

entries.title: Dio Accepts Every HTTP Response Status
entries.description: The response-status callback accepts every status for normal response processing rather than rejecting statuses through the client error path. Inspect how each caller handles unauthorized, forbidden and failed responses; callback acceptance does not prove an authorization bypass.
entries.impact: If callers treat rejected or failed responses as valid, they may make incorrect authorization or transaction decisions, process attacker-controlled error content, or conceal security-relevant failures.
entries.remediation:
Accept only the status codes expected by each operation. Handle authentication failures, redirects, and server errors explicitly before consuming response data or updating trusted state. Use platform trust and hostname validation and encrypted transport. Remove permissive callbacks and narrow necessary exceptions to the intended hosts.

Recommended actions:
1. Accept only the status codes expected by each operation. Handle authentication failures, redirects, and server errors explicitly before consuming response data or updating trusted state. Use platform trust and hostname validation and encrypted transport. Remove permissive callbacks and narrow necessary exceptions to the intended hosts.
entries.reviewer:
Trace handling of 401, 403 and transaction failures at each caller. Explicit application-side error handling can be legitimate; accepting a response is separate from trusting its body or authorizing an action.

Review steps:
1. Trace the matched candidate to its actual value, caller or resource.
2. Test invalid chains, wrong hostnames, redirects and build-specific exceptions; an unrelated trusted client or HTTPS URL does not protect this connection. Missing pinning alone is not proof of insecurity.
3. Resolve release configuration and runtime assumptions before confirming an issue.

entries.title: Hive Box Opened without Encryption
entries.description: Review target: Hive Box Opened Without Encryption. The application stores sensitive values or configures protection for persistent data. Determine the actual storage location, backup policy, and lock-state access restrictions. Determine whether the operation protects secrets, authenticates data or serves a non-security purpose; resolve algorithm, mode and key provenance.
entries.impact: An actor with access to unprotected application files, backups, or overly broad keychain access may recover credentials or private records and use them outside the intended trust boundary.
entries.remediation:
Use the platform credential or key store for secrets and appropriate authenticated encryption and file protection for private records. Minimize stored data, backup exposure, and lock-state accessibility. Use supported authenticated cryptography, securely generated keys and nonces, and platform-backed key storage; replace hardcoded or constant key material.

Recommended actions:
1. Store secrets using the platform credential store and apply appropriate access controls and protection to other private data.
2. Limit retention and unnecessary copies, configure backup handling deliberately, and verify access and recovery behavior in the deployed environment.
3. Use supported authenticated cryptography, securely generated keys and nonces, and platform-backed key storage; replace hardcoded or constant key material.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm Hive boxes containing sensitive data (tokens, PII, credentials) are opened with encryption. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent. Distinguish checksums from authentication, asymmetric RSA transformations from symmetric ECB, and test IV/nonce reuse, fixed keys and algorithm migration.

Review steps:
1. Identify the sensitive data, actual storage location, backup inclusion and lock-state or account access policy.
2. Inspect encryption, key access and data retention, including copies in caches, backups and exported artifacts.
3. Verify access under the relevant attacker model; a storage API alone does not establish an exposure.
4. Determine whether the operation protects secrets, authenticates data or serves a non-security purpose; resolve algorithm, mode and key provenance.
5. Distinguish checksums from authentication, asymmetric RSA transformations from symmetric ECB, and test IV/nonce reuse, fixed keys and algorithm migration.
6. Confirm reachability, the selected release build and the effect on a sensitive value before confirming an issue.

entries.title: Hive Uses a Constant Encryption Key
entries.description: The checked cryptographic configuration uses a constant embedded key, ECB mode, or a legacy algorithm. entries.title: WebView Navigation Policy Review

Recommended actions:
1. Limit the capability to the application’s required behavior and enforce the relevant runtime controls.
2. Verify the deployed artifact and add a regression check for the behavior that justified any correction.
3. Restrict schemes and parsed hosts, isolate external content, and validate messages and permissions on the native side.

entries.title: Local Secret Storage Review
entries.description: Review target: Ionic Storage Secret Marker. The application stores sensitive values or configures protection for persistent data. entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.

entries.title: SQL Query Construction Review
entries.description: The code constructs a query, selection, or ordering clause with values that may be externally controlled. Resolve whether those values enter syntax or bound data.
entries.impact: Attacker-controlled query syntax may change selected records, bypass intended filters, or modify stored data with the connection or provider’s privileges.

Recommended actions:

entries.title: Untrusted Input Entry Point
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code reads PHP request parameters or cookies. These are input entry points, not vulnerabilities by themselves.
entries.impact: If caller-controlled values reach a sensitive operation without suitable constraints, they may alter queries, filesystem paths, output or application state. The actual data flow and trust boundary must be established.
entries.remediation:
Validate expected types, lengths and allowed values. Apply destination-specific protection separately: SQL bindings, context-aware output encoding, path containment or a network destination policy.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep request validation separate from destination-specific controls.
2. Treat cookies as externally controlled even when the normal UI generates them.
entries.reviewer:
Follow the relevant $_GET, $_POST, $_REQUEST or $_COOKIE value to its use, including included files and stored values. Check authorization at the destination. Missing handlers or helper source leave the trace unresolved rather than establishing safety or exploitation.

Review steps:
1. Identify the specific external parameter.
2. Follow assignments and included helpers to its destination.
3. Check the protection at that use and record unresolved calls or missing source.

entries.title: OS Command Injection Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: A PHP process or shell operation is present. Review external influence over executable selection, command text and arguments.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Prefer a fixed executable and separate arguments through an API and runtime that support bypassing the shell. Allowlist operations and validate options. If a shell is unavoidable, verify argument escaping for the deployed operating system.

Recommended actions:
1. Use fixed operations and avoid shell command text where possible.
2. Constrain arguments and process privileges; escaping does not authorize an operation.
entries.reviewer:
Trace command text and backtick expressions into shell_exec, exec, passthru, system or popen. Verify whether a shell is used and assess argument injection as well as shell syntax. Establish the reachable caller and process privileges before confirming an issue.

Review steps:
1. Resolve the complete command and all external fragments.
2. Check shell invocation and argument parsing on the deployed operating system.
3. Test whether a caller can alter command structure or inject executable options.

entries.title: Dynamic Code Evaluation Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace externally influenced evaluation with fixed operations and data-only inputs. Use separate argument arrays for processes, allowlist permitted operations, and keep untrusted text out of executable templates or expressions.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Trace input flow into eval, exec, or assert sinks and verify that strict constraints prevent attacker-controlled execution. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Object Deserialization Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The application calls object-capable PHP deserialization. Identify the input trust and effective allowed_classes policy at this specific call; serialization alone and unrelated JSON decoding do not establish or mitigate object injection.
entries.impact: A crafted untrusted payload may instantiate dangerous types or trigger object behavior that executes code, modifies state, or exhausts resources when the parser permits those operations.
entries.remediation:
Use a data-only format and a safe loader for untrusted input. Disable automatic object or type construction, allowlist required types, and bound parsing size and complexity.

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.
entries.reviewer:
Trace whether untrusted input reaches unserialize or related deserialization paths and verify that class restrictions and payload trust checks are enforced. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Identify who can supply the matched input, including stored values and upstream services; record its type, size limits and trust boundary.
2. Trace the value through transformations to each sensitive operation. Check the protection at that destination and resource-level authorization.
3. Inspect the actual validation or protection implementation and its error path. A nearby keyword or a client-side check alone is insufficient evidence.

entries.title: Dynamic Code Evaluation Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: The rule identifies preg_replace code-evaluation or externally constructed pattern usage. The legacy /e modifier evaluated replacements and was removed in PHP 7; user-controlled patterns require a separate regex assessment.
entries.impact: If an attacker controls interpreted syntax or the operation selected, code or commands may run with the application’s privileges, allowing data theft, state changes, or service disruption.
entries.remediation:
Replace legacy /e expressions with preg_replace_callback and a fixed application callback. Use preg_quote with the correct delimiter for literal pattern data. Bound input and pattern complexity when user-defined expressions are intentional.

Recommended actions:
1. Use a fixed callback rather than executable replacement text.
2. Quote literal pattern data and set practical processing limits for configurable expressions.
entries.reviewer:
Verify PHP version, pattern delimiters, modifiers and replacement text. Separate legacy /e execution from regex injection or excessive backtracking. A fixed pattern or a runtime where /e is unavailable does not establish code execution.

Review steps:
1. Identify the full pattern and replacement.
2. Check whether the deployed PHP version supports /e evaluation.
3. Trace pattern and replacement control independently and assess the applicable execution or resource-use risk.

entries.title: HTML Output Encoding Review
entries.category: Untrusted Input Handling or Injection Flaws
entries.description: Application data is inserted into an HTML or script rendering context, or marked safe in a way that may bypass automatic encoding.
entries.impact: If attacker-controlled content reaches an executable browser context, it may run under the application’s origin, read accessible session data, or perform actions with the victim’s permissions.
entries.remediation:

Recommended actions:
1. Use server-side type, length and allowed-value checks appropriate to the input. For free-form text, preserve legitimate characters and protect each destination separately.
2. Bind database values as parameters, encode output for its rendering context, and constrain file or network destinations where applicable. Test rejected input and unauthorized access.

entries.title: Redirect Destination Review
entries.description: The code handles a link, redirect, or externally selected navigation target. Validate the effective destination and any action triggered by the receiving handler.
entries.impact: A crafted destination or link may direct users to a phishing site, leak URL-carried secrets, or trigger unauthorized operations if routing trusts external parameters without the required access checks.
entries.remediation:
Allowlist schemes, hosts, paths, and operations. Validate parsed link parameters, avoid credentials in URLs, and require authentication and authorization before sensitive actions.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer application route identifiers mapped to fixed destinations; permit only necessary relative paths or explicitly allowed external destinations.
2. Reject unsupported schemes and ambiguous destinations and test redirect handling after decoding and normalization.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect Location header construction and validation controls for open redirect risk. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether untrusted input controls the redirect destination and whether the redirect is reachable.
2. Inspect URL parsing, relative versus absolute destinations, scheme handling and authorization around the redirect.
3. Check how encoded or ambiguous URLs are interpreted by the framework and browser before confirming an unsafe redirect.

entries.title: File Inclusion Review
entries.description: The code includes or requires a PHP file. Review external influence over the selected path and stream wrapper.
entries.impact: An attacker controlling a path or shared file may read or replace private files, delete data, or redirect an operation outside its intended directory if containment and access controls are ineffective.

Recommended actions:
1. Select includes through fixed mappings.
2. Keep uploads and writable content outside executable include paths.
entries.reviewer:
Trace the include operand through configuration and helpers. Determine whether an attacker can select a local file, uploaded PHP content or a remote wrapper supported by the runtime. Fixed application includes do not establish inclusion abuse.

Review steps:
1. Resolve the final include or require operand.
2. Check canonical path containment and permitted file mappings.
3. Inspect wrappers, writable destinations and reachable attacker control.

entries.description: Externally supplied array keys may be converted into local variable names.
entries.impact: An attacker may overwrite security-relevant variables or alter program decisions when imported keys collide with trusted local state.

entries.title: File Path and Access Review
entries.description: The code accesses, creates, deletes, or shares filesystem data. Resolve path provenance, destination containment, permission modes, and any concurrent access.
entries.impact: An attacker controlling a path or shared file may read or replace private files, delete data, or redirect an operation outside its intended directory if containment and access controls are ineffective.
entries.remediation:
Resolve paths beneath a fixed permitted root and verify containment and effective permissions. Use safe exclusive temporary-file creation, restrict sharing, and account for symlinks and concurrent changes.

Recommended actions:
1. Resolve paths against a fixed permitted root and enforce containment with filesystem-aware checks; avoid simple prefix checks.
2. Use application-controlled file identifiers where possible, restrict filesystem privileges, and test traversal and archive extraction boundaries.
entries.reviewer:
Inspect file path construction in fopen, file_get_contents, and file_put_contents flows and validate path controls. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Trace external influence over the path and resolve it as the filesystem will, including relative segments and symbolic links.
2. Check the resolved destination remains within the permitted root and that the caller is authorized for the specific file operation.
3. Inspect read, write and extraction paths separately; record the effective path restrictions and deployment permissions.

entries.title: Error Detail Disclosure Review
entries.description: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Log only the operational details needed, redact sensitive values, and return limited error messages to clients.
2. Restrict diagnostic and log access and test production error responses and representative log output.
entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched path logs sensitive data or exposes diagnostics to an untrusted recipient.
2. Trace the actual values, redaction and error handling, including production configuration and log retention or access.
3. Distinguish internal operational diagnostics from client-visible output and record the reachable disclosure path without reproducing secrets.

entries.title: Legacy PHP API Review
entries.description: The source references a dependency, version, or deprecated API. Resolve the actual deployed version and supported behavior before deciding whether it needs replacement.
entries.impact: A reachable vulnerability in an unsupported or affected dependency may compromise the application with its privileges. A version declaration or deprecated API alone does not establish that such a vulnerability is present.
entries.remediation:
Inventory resolved dependencies and runtime versions, compare them with authoritative advisories and support policy, and migrate affected or unsupported components to tested supported replacements.

Recommended actions:
1. Replace unsupported APIs or affected dependencies with a supported option after checking application compatibility.
2. Pin and verify the deployed version and test the affected behavior and error paths after the update.
entries.reviewer:
Locate deprecated API usage and validate migration completeness to secure alternatives. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:

entries.title: XML External Entity Review
entries.description: The code parses or transforms XML. Resolve external entity, DTD, and resource-loading settings for the actual parser instance.

1. Apply the rule-specific correction above only after verifying the affected behavior and required control.

entries.title: TLS Certificate Validation Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a transport-security exception, insecure endpoint, or certificate-validation configuration. Resolve the effective policy and the connections it governs.

entries.title: Debug Mode Configuration Review
entries.description: A configuration or API enables development diagnostics, process inspection, or debugging. Verify whether it applies to a deployed production artifact.
entries.impact: An actor with access to an enabled debugging interface may inspect private state or influence application execution; exposed development endpoints may disclose internal implementation details.

Recommended actions:
1. Disable development-only functionality in production and enforce the environment boundary in deployment configuration.
2. Restrict operational diagnostics and add a production-configuration check covering the exposed route or feature.
entries.reviewer:
Verify deployment profiles do not enable debug/reload. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

1. Inspect the effective production configuration and determine who can reach debugging or development functionality.

entries.title: Object Deserialization Review
entries.description: The application reads serialized objects or uses a parser that may construct runtime types. Identify the input’s trust and the effective parser and type restrictions.
entries.impact: A crafted untrusted payload may instantiate dangerous types or trigger object behavior that executes code, modifies state, or exhausts resources when the parser permits those operations.
entries.remediation:
Use a data-only format and a safe loader for untrusted input. Disable automatic object or type construction, allowlist required types, and bound parsing size and complexity.

Recommended actions:
1. Prefer a data-only format mapped to explicit application types; avoid reconstructing arbitrary runtime objects from untrusted input.
2. Restrict allowed types and converters, limit input size and nesting, and test rejection of unexpected type metadata.
entries.reviewer:

entries.title: SQL Injection Review
entries.description: The checked source contains a database query or query-construction operation. Determine whether untrusted values can change statement structure and whether record access is authorized.
entries.impact: If externally controlled values enter query syntax, an attacker may read, change, or delete records or bypass data-access restrictions with the database connection’s privileges. Fixed queries and correctly bound parameters do not establish this condition.

Recommended actions:

entries.title: Cross-Origin Access Policy Review
entries.description: A browser-origin or navigation policy permits a broad set of external origins or destinations. Identify the resources and privileged interfaces covered by the effective policy.
entries.impact: An untrusted site may read protected responses or invoke privileged interfaces if a permissive policy admits it and independent authentication or authorization does not prevent the operation.

Recommended actions:
1. Allow only the origins and browser capabilities required by the application; avoid reflecting arbitrary origins.

entries.reviewer:

Review steps:
1. Inspect the effective origin policy together with credentials, allowed methods and headers, including environment overrides.

entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.

entries.title: OS Command Injection Review
entries.description: The code invokes an interpreter, process, dynamic expression, or template-execution mechanism. Trace executable selection and evaluated content to their trust boundaries.

entries.title: GCP Storage Bucket Publicly Accessible
entries.description: Storage configuration may permit public object access. Resolve bucket or container policies, object ACLs, and provider-level public-access controls.

entries.title: Network Access Policy Review
entries.description: The code uses a low-level memory, formatting, allocation, or type-conversion operation whose safety depends on bounds, types, initialization, and caller invariants.
entries.impact: A violated memory or formatting invariant may expose process memory, corrupt application state, crash the process, or permit code execution when an attacker can influence the relevant inputs.
entries.remediation:
Validate sizes and types before use, use bounded and type-safe APIs, and keep format strings fixed. Prefer checked conversions and safe ownership abstractions; document and test every remaining unsafe invariant.

Recommended actions:
1. Use bounded operations, checked size calculations and explicit ownership or automatic resource management appropriate to the language.
2. Test boundary sizes and failure paths; use memory diagnostics where available to verify the specific correction.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm open CIDR rules are intentional and that exposed services have appropriate application-layer controls. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Inspect buffer capacity, index bounds, integer conversions and ownership at the matched operation and its callers.
2. Check initialization, aliases, lifetime and cleanup on success, exception and early-return paths; identify external influence over sizes or values.
3. Verify a concrete unsafe access or lifetime condition. A low-level API or allocation alone does not prove memory corruption.

entries.description: Storage encryption is disabled or not established by the checked configuration. Resolve provider defaults and the effective deployed encryption policy.
entries.impact: Someone who obtains unauthorized access to underlying storage or snapshots may recover private records without the intended encryption-at-rest boundary.
entries.remediation:
Enable appropriate storage and snapshot encryption with controlled key access. Verify the effective deployed state and plan migration of existing unencrypted data.

Recommended actions:

2. Limit retention and unnecessary copies, configure backup handling deliberately, and verify access and recovery behavior in the deployed environment.

2. Inspect encryption, key access and data retention, including copies in caches, backups and exported artifacts.
3. Verify access under the relevant attacker model; a storage API alone does not establish an exposure.

entries.title: CloudTrail Logging Disabled
entries.description: The code writes diagnostic data or exposes detailed errors. Establish the values emitted, production configuration, and recipients of the output.
entries.impact: Readers of exposed diagnostics may obtain credentials, private records, internal paths, or implementation details that enable account misuse or targeted attacks.
entries.remediation:
Keep sensitive values and detailed errors out of user-facing responses and routine logs. Redact before emission, restrict diagnostic access, and verify production logging configuration.

Recommended actions:
1. Log only the operational details needed, redact sensitive values, and return limited error messages to clients.
2. Restrict diagnostic and log access and test production error responses and representative log output.

3. Distinguish internal operational diagnostics from client-visible output and record the reachable disclosure path without reproducing secrets.

entries.title: Hardcoded Credential or Secret Review
entries.description: The checked source or build configuration embeds potentially sensitive credential or key material. Determine whether it is active and whether it reaches distributed artifacts or logs.
entries.impact: A party who can read exposed source, artifacts, configuration, or logs may recover active secrets and access the protected service or decrypt data with the secret owner’s privileges.
entries.remediation:
Remove active secrets from source and build layers, rotate exposed values, and load replacements through a restricted secret-management facility. Use narrowly privileged, short-lived credentials.

Recommended actions:
1. Keep real secrets out of source and public artifacts; obtain them through the deployment secret mechanism with restricted access.
2. If a credential has been exposed, revoke or rotate it and verify that old values no longer work; remove accidental logging and add a regression check.
entries.reviewer:
Confirm all credential values reference variables or data sources, not literal strings. This can be confirmed as an issue when the matched path is reachable and required controls are missing, weak, or inconsistent.

Review steps:
1. Determine whether the matched value is a real credential, key or token rather than a placeholder, public identifier or test fixture.
2. Inspect how it is used and where it is exposed, including source history, build artifacts, logs and deployment configuration.
3. Record the affected service and privileges without copying secret values into the review report.
